item.title: Homotopy types and torsion in homology of generalized chessboard complexes
item.description: arXiv:2610.37827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiple chessboard complexes are deleted joins of skeleta of a simplex. We classify their homotopy types for at most three rows and extend this classification to arbitrary column capacities, with the $2$-torus as the only exception to a wedge of spheres. We determine explicit homotopy decompositions for two families with four and five rows and use a common capacity redistribution map to construct infinite families with $2$- and $3$-torsion in integral homology. Together, these results give a negative answer to the Segre part of the problem posed by Reiner and Roberts on characteristic-free resolutions of Segre and Veronese modules and identify three as the largest number of rows for which all generalized chessboard complexes have torsion-free integral homology. Our $3$-torsion construction applies to every square ordinary chessboard complex with at least five rows. Combined with earlier results, it completes the proof of the Shareshian-Wachs conjecture on torsion in chessboard complexes.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Limonchenko, Seonghyeon Yu

item.title: High-chromatic tournament parts without a complete pair of cyclic triangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour conjectured that any two disjoint subtournaments of sufficiently large chromatic number contain cyclic triangles, one in each subtournament, with all edges between them oriented in the same direction. We disprove this conjecture by constructing, for every positive integer $d$, a tournament $T$ with a vertex partition $(X,Y)$ such that $\chi(T[X]),\chi(T[Y])\ge d$, but no cyclic triangle in either part is complete to a cyclic triangle in the other. Our construction combines a graph of large girth and large chromatic number with a variant of Kneser graphs defined in terms of binary functions. We give two proofs of the required chromatic lower bound, one using the Borsuk--Ulam theorem and the other using the octahedral form of Tucker's lemma.
item.dc:creator: Guantao Chen, Hein van der Holst, Shengze Wang

item.title: Generalised hyperbolic polynomials: combinatorial interpretation and real-rootedness
item.description: arXiv:2610.37931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $p,q$ natural numbers, define $\Delta^{\langle p,q \rangle}:=x^{p-1}\frac{\partial}{\partial y} + y^{q-1}\frac{\partial}{\partial x}$, and consider the sequence of polynomials $\biggl((\Delta^{\langle p,q \rangle})^n \cdot x\biggr)_{n\geq 0}$; we call these the generalised hyperbolic polynomials. In this paper, we provide a simple combinatorial interpretation for these polynomials. As special cases, we obtain combinatorial interpretations for the coefficients of the analogs of sinh and cosh corresponding to the curve $x^p- p y^q/q=1$; on setting $p=q=3$, we obtain Conrad and Flajolet's tree interpretation for the coefficients of the Dixonian elliptic functions (2006) as a special case. Finally, we show that for any $p,q\geq 3$, after suitably normalising followed by substituting $y=1$, we obtain a sequence of univariate polynomials which are real-rooted.
item.dc:creator: Bishal Deb

item.title: Non-associative Hopf Algebra on Dyck Paths Arising from the Shuffle-insertion Product
item.description: arXiv:2610.38139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we define a shuffle-insertion product and a cut-box coproduct on the vector space spanned by Dyck paths, where the product is commutative but non-associative. We prove that the product and coproduct are compatible, making the space a non-associative bialgebra. This bialgebra is connected and bigraded by path degree and peak number, and hence is a non-associative Hopf algebra. Its primitive subspace is spanned by atoms, and associators of primitive elements are primitive. Furthermore, we provide closed-form formulas for its left and right antipodes. We also define the convolution product on the space of linear transformations of the non-associative Hopf algebra, which equips this space with a non-associative algebra structure. Finally, we construct a one-parameter deformation preserving the cut-box coproduct. Its zero specialization is the ordinary shuffle Hopf algebra, which is also the associated graded algebra for the atom filtration, while every nonzero specialization is isomorphic to the shuffle-insertion algebra.
item.dc:creator: Nantel Bergeron, Yuchen Guo, Huilan Li

item.title: Inflection sets of permutations
item.description: arXiv:2610.38237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2020, Brualdi and Dahl introduced the discrete derivative $\sigma'(i)=\sigma(i+1)-\sigma(i)$ of a permutation $\sigma\in\Sym_n$. In this paper, we focus on the second derivative of a permutation, $\sigma''(i)=\sigma(i+1)+\sigma(i-1)-2\sigma(i)$, and the inflections it determines. We show that for even $n$, the only distinct permutations with the same second derivative are the identity and its reverse, while for odd $n$, the second derivative is not injective even after excluding them. We then study which sets of pairs of integers $(i,j)$ are the inflection set of some permutation and whether a given set is witnessed in $\Sym_n$ for infinitely many $n$. We show that exactly $14$ permutations of $[n]$ have no inflections when $n\ge5$. For a single inflection $\{(k,m)\}$, we determine all $n$ for which it is witnessed in $\Sym_n$: we prove it is always witnessed, and it is witnessed for only finitely many $n$ if and only if $m\ge 2k+1$. In that case, all such $n$ satisfy $2m-2k+1\le n\le 2m-k+2$ (apart from $k=2$, $n=m+1$), and, perhaps surprisingly, this range has gaps once $k\ge 10$, the smallest occurring at $(k,m,n)=(10,21,30)$. Finally, we characterize maximally inflected permutations, whose second derivative alternates in sign, and show that their number $|\mathcal M_n|$ satisfies $2E_n\le|\mathcal M_n|\le(2/3)^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1}\,n!$, where $E_n$ is the Euler zigzag number.
item.dc:creator: Gordon Rojas Kirby, Mariana Smit Vega Garcia

item.title: A Characterization of Functions on the Integer Lattice That Are L-Extendable through Local Convex Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: L-extendable functions on the integer lattice are functions that admit a $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxation; that is, values can be assigned to the additional half-integral points, while keeping the original values at integer points, so that the resulting function is $\frac12$UJ-convex. Various examples of L-extendable functions and their applications are known. A general characterization of L-extendability for functions on the integer lattice, however, remains open. In this paper, we study the L-extendability of functions on the integer lattice. We first obtain a necessary condition: L-extendable functions are integrally convex. We then consider a special subclass of L-extendable functions, namely, those whose local convex extensions give L-convex relaxations. This subclass has a useful optimization property: the optimal value of the original function coincides with that of the $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxation given by its local convex extension, a property not guaranteed for general $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxations. We characterize this subclass by showing that a function is L-extendable through its local convex extension if and only if it is integrally convex and its restriction to every unit hypercube is D-convex, where D-convexity is a discrete convexity associated with reflected Freudenthal simplicial divisions. This subclass strictly contains the class of D-convex functions. We also give a combinatorial characterization of D-convex subsets of the vertices of a unit hypercube: a set $X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ is D-convex if and only if it is majority-closed and contains a relative opposite pair.
item.dc:creator: Ken Yokoyama, Yuni Iwamasa, Kei Kimura

item.title: Determination of weight enumerators of binary extremal self-dual codes of length 60
item.description: arXiv:2610.38323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct three binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$ with weight enumerators for which no binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$ were previously known to exist. This completes the determination of the weight enumerators that occur for binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$.
item.dc:creator: Masaaki Harada

item.title: Sizes of cross-intersecting families
item.description: arXiv:2610.38328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The size of cross-intersecting families ${\cal F}_1, \dots, {\cal F}_d$ is usually measured by the sum or the product of the sizes $|{\cal F}_i|$. These two natural size functions have different extremal structures, and different techniques have been developed for them. We introduce the cross-degree of a size function and show that the potential extremal structures of maximum cross-intersecting families are the same for all size functions of finite cross-degree, including the sum and the product. Our main tool is a strengthened form of the generating family method of Ahlswede--Khachatrian, based on standard generating families and on local modifications of cross-intersecting families, which we call mutations. It treats two completely different types of extremal structures in a unified way and, unlike the original method, needs shifting in only one step.
item.dc:creator: Ziqing Xiang, Huajun Zhang

item.title: Crescent configurations in three dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A crescent configuration of $n$ points in $\mathbb R^d$ is a set in general position whose distinct pairwise distances have multiplicities $1,\ldots,n-1$. We construct such a configuration in $\mathbb R^3$ for every $n\geq3$, giving a uniform bound of three for the minimum dimension. The proof uses equally spaced parameters on a short circular helix and Rolle's theorem. We also give explicit integer-coordinate configurations with $O(n\log n)$ bits per coordinate, and prove that every finite initial segment of the sequence $(\cos j,\sin j,2j)_{j\geq0}$ of length at least three is a crescent configuration.
item.dc:creator: Yuda Chen

item.title: A logarithmic error term for subset sums of zero-sum-free sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.38373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a positive integer $k$, let $f(k)$ be the minimum number of distinct nonempty subset sums of a zero-sum-free $k$-element set, where the minimum is taken over all finite abelian groups. We prove $f(k)\ge \frac{k^2}{2}-13k\log(k+1)-116k$. Together with the classical upper bound, this gives $f(k)=k^2/2+O(k\log k)$, with the optimal leading coefficient. As a consequence, the Olson constant of every finite abelian group $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{Ol}(G)\le\sqrt{2|G|}+O(\log|G|)$. The argument combines a triangular lower bound for repeated supports, a count using blocks of two and three copies, and a greedy expansion argument. No restriction is imposed on the order of the group or on the stabilizer of the set of subset sums.
item.dc:creator: Chao Liu

item.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.38386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14{,}639{,}440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Elliott Mathewson

item.title: Nice Partitions of Signed-Graphic Arrangements Are Inductive Factorizations
item.description: arXiv:2610.38412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nice partitions of hyperplane arrangements give tensor factorizations of Orlik-Solomon algebras as graded vector spaces. In general, a hyperplane arrangement admitting a nice partition need not be free. In this paper, we consider signed-graphic arrangements, the subarrangements of type-$B$ Weyl arrangements, over fields of characteristic different from $2$. We prove that every nice partition of a signed-graphic arrangement is an inductive factorization and hence that the arrangement is free, with nonzero exponents given by the part sizes. In particular, Terao's conjecture holds for the intersection lattices of signed-graphic arrangements admitting a nice partition.
item.dc:creator: Weikang Liang, Suijie Wang, Yue Zhou

item.title: Tur\'an number of three disjoint cliques of arbitrary sizes
item.description: arXiv:2610.38430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Tur\'an number $\rm ex(n,H)$ of a given graph $H$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $H$-free graph. In this paper, for all $p\ge q\ge r\ge 2$ and $n\geq p+q+r$, we determine the exact value of $\rm ex(n,K_p\cup K_q\cup K_r)$ and describe all extremal graphs.
item.dc:creator: Alexandr Kostochka, Dadong Peng, Zimu Xiang, Liang Zhang

item.title: Davenport constants with growing binary rank
item.description: arXiv:2610.38447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the correction to the standard lower bound $D^*$ for Davenport constants of finite abelian groups with a growing elementary two-component. For every fixed nontrivial abelian $p$-group $H$ of odd order, we prove $D(H\oplus C_2^r)=D^*(H\oplus C_2^r)+(D(H)-1)\log_2 r+O_H(1)$, with a uniform version for varying $H$. For $C_3\oplus C_2^r$, we determine exact values on explicit infinite intervals of ranks. More generally, the correction is logarithmic or smaller precisely when the fixed group has at most one odd prime divisor. We show that the two-primary part affects the logarithmic coefficient: for $C_{24}\oplus C_2^r$, the ratio $(D-D^*)/\log_2 r$ has limsup at least $2.4933231\ldots>2$, whereas for $C_3\oplus C_2^r$ the limit is $2$. These upper limiting coefficients are unbounded even with the odd prime fixed. The proofs use binary codes and finite-field Fourier analysis.
item.dc:creator: Chao Liu

item.title: Hilbert functions of filtered graphical zonotopal algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.38469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The external zonotopal algebra of a graph is generated by nilpotent vertex elements $X_v$ and determines the graphical matroid after deleting loops. Replacing these generators by $f(X_v)$, for a power series $f(u)$, and filtering by word length gives a family of filtered algebras. We extend filtered graph reconstruction from simple graphs to loopless multigraphs without isolated vertices when the linear and quadratic coefficients of $f$ are nonzero. Nevertheless, even the family of Hilbert functions indexed by all polynomials does not determine the graph: two nonisomorphic ten-vertex trees have the same Hilbert function for every $f$, answering a question of Nenashev and the first author. For forests and series whose first nonconstant term has degree $k\ge 2$, we give a monomial presentation indexed by partial score vectors whose entries are divisible by $k$. For normalized nondegenerate functions, a boundary-state calculus gives a common finite parameter partition for all trees of a fixed maximum degree. In maximum degrees three and four, exact symbolic calculations identify these partitions by the vanishing of specified coefficients of $f^{-1}$. For functions with nonzero quadratic coefficient, the same calculus gives explicit recurrences for attached or connecting paths. Symmetry reductions, including commuting actions of $sl_2$ and the symmetric group on the leaves of a star, determine the generic Hilbert series of stars and two-vertex multigraphs and also apply to parallel edges and leaves in larger graphs. For cycles, we determine the highest-degree term and the first three nonconstant coefficients in the stable range. A weighted independent-set formula describes the trace sequence in the remaining conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Boris Shapiro, Ilya Smirnov, Arkady Vaintrob

item.title: EKR Results for Cuspidal Representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}_\chi$ be a cuspidal representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$. A subset $S \subseteq \mathrm{GL}_2(q)$ is \emph{$t$-intersecting} if $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\{v \in \mathcal{S}_\chi: g_1v = g_2v\} \geqslant t$ for any $g_1, g_2 \in S$. In this paper, we determine $\max{|S|}$ where $S$ is $t$-intersecting.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqi Liao

item.title: The asymptotics of off-diagonal book Ramsey numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.38515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $B_n$ be the book graph consisting of $n$ triangles sharing a common edge. We prove upper bounds for $r(B_{\lceil\alpha n\rceil},B_n)$ that asymptotically match the known lower bounds in the remaining range $1/6<\alpha<1/4$. Combined with the known results for the other ranges of $\alpha$, this completely determines the asymptotics of the Ramsey number $r(B_{\lceil\alpha n\rceil},B_n)$ for every fixed $0<\alpha\le1$: \[ r(B_{\lceil\alpha n\rceil},B_n)=(c(\alpha)+o(1))n, \qquad c(\alpha)= \begin{cases} 2, & 0<\alpha\le1/6,\\[1mm] \displaystyle\frac{3}{1+2p_\alpha^2}, & 1/6<\alpha\le\alpha_0,\\[3mm] (1+\sqrt\alpha)^2, & \alpha_0<\alpha\le1, \end{cases} \] where \(\alpha_0:=\frac{52-16\sqrt3}{121}, \;\; p_\alpha:=\frac{1-\sqrt{\alpha(3-2\alpha)}}{1-2\alpha} \;\; (1/6<\alpha\le\alpha_0).\) Consequently, the random lower bound is asymptotically tight if and only if $\alpha\ge\alpha_0$, thereby determining exactly the range of $\alpha$ for which the conjecture of Conlon, Fox and Wigderson holds. The proof develops a defect-compensation framework around a $K_4$-free auxiliary graph.
item.dc:creator: Lulu Dai, Chunchao Fan, Qizhong Lin

item.title: Minimizing the spectral radius of unicyclic graphs with fixed order and dissociation number
item.description: arXiv:2610.38539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A dissociation set of a graph G is a vertex subset S contained in V(G) such that the induced subgraph G[S] has maximum degree at most 1, and the dissociation number of G is the cardinality of a maximum dissociation set denoted by {\Phi}(G). In this paper, we first derive a sharp lower bound on the dissociation number for all unicyclic graphs. Furthermore, we also study the graphs with minimum spectral radius among all unicyclic graphs with given order and dissociation number and explicitly identify all extremal graphs for \(n-4 \le \Phi(G) \le n-1\).
item.dc:creator: Yu Zhou, Yuanyuan Chen, Dan Li, Dandan Fan

item.title: Directed isoperimetry and infinitely fast robbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.38552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the fast version of the cops and robber game on finite digraphs with unit-speed cops and an unbounded-speed robber. We prove a lower bound for the cop number of every strongly connected digraph in terms of its order, maximum out-degree, and out-vertex expansion, extending Mehrabian's isoperimetric lower bound to digraphs, where connected components are replaced by forward reachable sets. For strongly connected abelian Cayley digraphs of fixed out-degree, we show that the ratio of the cop number to the number of vertices is comparable to each of out-vertex expansion, vertex expansion of the underlying undirected graph, minimum nontrivial character displacement, the square root of the unnormalized Laplacian spectral gap of the underlying undirected graph, and the reciprocal of its diameter. The comparison constants depend polynomially on the out-degree. In the undirected case, we also compare pathwidth with these parameters, complementing the bounded-degree treewidth comparison of Alon and Mehrabian. Combining the directed lower bound with recent cyclic sweep techniques for abelian Cayley graphs, we determine the order of the cop number of positively oriented tori and directed Heisenberg graphs.
item.dc:creator: Arindam Biswas

item.title: Large tight components and Dirac thresholds for tight Hamilton cycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.38560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every odd integer $r\ge1$, let $q_r=1-2^{-r}\binom r{(r-1)/2}$. We show that, for every odd $r\ge3$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph with at least $q_r\binom nr$ edges contains a tight component with at least $(1/2-o(1))\binom nr$ edges. This confirms a conjecture posed by Lang and Sanhueza-Matamala in 2024. As an application, for every odd $r\ge1$ and every integer $k\ge\lceil r(3-2q_r)\rceil$, we prove that the asymptotic minimum $(k-r)$-degree threshold for a tight Hamilton cycle in a $k$-uniform hypergraph is $q_r$, which settles, in this range, another conjecture of Lang and Sanhueza-Matamala in 2022 stating that the lower-bound construction due to Han and Zhao is asymptotically optimal. Our proof combines an isoperimetric inequality for Johnson graphs with a Kruskal-Katona-type theorem, which is of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Hao Lin, Guanghui Wang, Jiande Zhang, Wenling Zhou

item.title: The exact digirth and out-degree bounds for $C(k,k)$-subdivision and out-forest in digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.38574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each integer $k\ge2$, let $C(k,k)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by two internally vertex-disjoint directed paths of length $k$ with the same initial and terminal vertices. Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud ({\small European J. Combin., 2024}) asked for the smallest integer $g_k$ such that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least two and digirth at least $g_k$ contains a subdivision of $C(k,k)$. We completely resolve this problem by proving that $g_k=k+1$. Our proof relies on a refinement of Thomassen's theorem ({\small Discrete Math., 1985}) on two directed cycles intersecting in exactly one vertex: we prove that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least two contains two directed cycles intersecting in exactly one arc. We also establish an embedding theorem for out-forests with prescribed images of their roots, under minimum out-degree and digirth conditions determined by the number of leaves and the heights of vertices in antichains. As an application, for integers $k,\ell\ge2$, we show that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least \(k\) and digirth at least \(k(\ell-1)+1\) contains \(k\) directed paths of length \(\ell\) sharing only their initial vertex, which can be prescribed arbitrarily. This improves the previous digirth bound \((k^\ell-1)/(k-1)+1\) of Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud to a sharp bound.
item.dc:creator: Bin Chen, Jianfeng Hou, Xinmin Hou, Siyue Liu, Xinjie Wang, Xinyu Zhou

item.title: Graphon Colourings and Limits of Graph Partitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a framework for pure and mixed graphon colourings and use it to study the limiting behaviour of graph partition parameters under cut convergence. Pure colourings correspond to measurable partitions, while mixed colourings assign a probability distribution on the colour set to each point. We develop the representation, equivalence and convergence theory, and show that every mixed graphon colouring has an equivalent pure representative, possibly on a different probability space. For each fixed finite colour set, we establish compactness and describe the topology of coloured graph limits using the cut norm on graphons and the weak-$*$ topology on colourings. The usual coloured cut distance characterises convergence for pure colourings, but not for general mixed colourings. As applications, we prove that the Cheeger constant and modularity converge to their mixed graphon counterparts along cut-convergent graph sequences whose orders tend to infinity, assuming uniformly linear minimum degree and positive limiting edge density, respectively. Both mixed functionals are invariant under graphon equivalence. We also establish their continuity in cut distance on the corresponding classes of graphons, with a stability bound for the Cheeger constant. For modularity, we further characterise coloured graphons attaining extremal modularity values and prove attainment of the mixed optimum for each fixed number of colours. We also exhibit a graphon whose modularity supremum is not attained by any finite colouring.
item.dc:creator: Svante Janson, Tiffany Y. Y. Lo, Colin McDiarmid, Anda Skeja, Fiona Skerman

item.title: Larger Crossing Families
item.description: arXiv:2610.38658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give the first explicit constant for crossing families of linear size by showing that every set of $n$ points in general position in the plane contains a crossing family of size approximately $\frac{n}{79}$. We further identify some conditions where there are even larger crossing families. The first such condition forbids the existence of a large different pattern, namely non-convex 4-clusters: We show that every point set contains either a large non-convex 4-cluster or a large crossing family. The second condition is the existence of many crossings: We give a bound for the size of a crossing family in terms of the number of crossings of the complete geometric graph drawn on the point set.
item.dc:creator: Joachim Orthaber, Patrick Schnider

item.title: Simple Cuts, Simple Landscapes: Global Synchronization and Rank-Width-One Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.38670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how the structure of the coupling matrix $\boldsymbol A$ shapes the energy landscape $E_{\boldsymbol A}(\boldsymbol\theta)=-\frac12\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}\cos(\theta_i-\theta_j)$ of the Kuramoto model. We prove that, for an entrywise nonnegative coupling matrix $\boldsymbol A$ with connected support, if $\boldsymbol A$ has rank-width one over $\mathbb R$, then the landscape is "simple", i.e., every local minimum is synchronized. The rank-width bound is sharp, and the result has many interesting implications for global synchronization. The key contribution of this work is to uncover a structural synchronization mechanism beyond the rank-one regime, which has served as a starting point for earlier analyses of global synchronization.
item.dc:creator: Hongjin Wu

item.title: Projected Brion's theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.38674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an analogue of Brion's theorem for the projected integer-point transform. Brion's theorem writes the integer-point transform of a rational polyhedron $P$ as the sum of the rational functions associated to its vertex cones. The pushforward $\pi_*$ along a lattice projection $\pi$ turns the transform of $P$ into the generating function of the numbers of lattice points in the fibres of $\pi$. We group the vertices of $P$ into contracted classes, generated by the edges whose direction $\pi$ kills, and show that the sum of the rational functions associated to the vertex cones in a contracted class can be pushed forward along $\pi$, yielding a rational function decomposition of the projected integer-point transform. For a lattice polytope, the classes correspond to the connected components of the fixed locus of the associated toric variety under the action of a subtorus, and our formula resembles the localization formula for this subtorus. We use this decomposition to provide an explicit formula for the projected integer-point transform of a linear family of polytopes. We illustrate this result with families of Gelfand--Zetlin and string polytopes.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Dupraz, Leonid Monin

item.title: Primitive flag-transitive generalized quadrangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.38819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a finite thick generalized quadrangle of order $(s,t)$ with a flag-transitive automorphism group $G$. A well-known conjecture of Kantor from the early 1990s asserts that up to duality, $\mathcal{Q}$ is either of classical type, or it is one of two sporadic examples of order $(3,5)$ or $(15,17)$. Although this fundamental problem in finite geometry remains open, it has been resolved in some special cases. For example, a theorem of Buekenhout and Van Maldeghem from 1994 proves Kantor's conjecture under the stronger assumption that $G$ acts distance-transitively on the set of points of $\mathcal{Q}$. In this paper, we study Kantor's conjecture in the setting where $G$ acts primitively on both the points and lines of $\mathcal{Q}$. Here a theorem of Bamberg et al. implies that $G$ is almost simple with socle $X$ a finite simple group of Lie type, and several special cases where the Lie rank of $X$ is at most $2$ have recently been settled in a sequence of papers. Our main theorem resolves the problem for all almost simple groups of Lie type, thereby completing the proof of Kantor's conjecture for generalized quadrangles with a flag-transitive automorphism group acting primitively on points and lines.
item.dc:creator: Timothy C. Burness, Tao Feng, Jianbing Lu

item.title: Extended weak order in all rank three Coxeter groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.38849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that extended weak order is a lattice for all rank 3 Coxeter groups. This was previously known in finite and affine types, and in the universal Coxeter group of rank 3. All other cases are new to this paper. As in earlier work, the proof proceeds by showing that all rank 3 Coxeter arrangements are clean arrangements, meaning that every biclosed set is weakly separated from its complement by a hyperplane. As a consequence, we also deduce Dyer's Conjecture A for all rank 3 Coxeter groups, which asserts that cover relations in extended weak order are given by toggling a single root.
item.dc:creator: Grant Barkley, Colin Defant, Patricia Hersh, Jon McCammond, Thomas McConville, David E Speyer

item.title: Graftings and cograftings for species
item.description: arXiv:2610.38996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce graftings and cograftings for vector species, modelled on the elementary operations of adjoining and deleting a root in a rooted forest. We relate these maps to operads, up and down operators, and obtain nontrivial balanced pairs, admitting pair of creation/annihilation operators with commuting relations. We establish universal properties for the species of rooted forests. Using Fock functors, we recover the classical Connes--Kreimer Hopf algebra, its noncommutative planar analogue, and Foissy's $q$-infinitesimal Hopf algebra.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Clavier, Yannic Vargas

item.title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
item.description: arXiv:2610.39021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive. The main tool is a positivity statement for products: a product of Kazhdan-Lusztig positive immanants of complementary submatrices is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive, which we deduce at $q=1$ from Braden's hyperbolic localization, following Billey and Braden. With Haiman's theorem for irreducible characters, it shows that every class function whose Frobenius characteristic lies in the semiring generated by Schur functions and hook monomial symmetric functions is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive; for example, Skandera's chain of normalised hook immanants is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive for every $n$. We place these results in a comparison of three cones of class functions, and show that the remaining obstructions to Haiman's conjecture lie at singular Schubert varieties that are not reached by an iterated doubling identity of Abreu and Nigro, for which we give an explicit criterion. Finally, on the full span of permutation monomials, an element that is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices can have a negative coefficient at the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanant $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ if and only if the Schubert variety $X_w$ is singular; Skandera proved the smooth half.
item.dc:creator: Keith McNulty

item.title: A proof of the Murty--Simon conjecture on diameter-$2$-critical graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Murty-Simon conjecture states that every $n$-vertex diameter-$2$-critical graph has at most $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ edges, with equality only for the balanced complete bipartite graph. Using regularity methods, F\"uredi proved this for all sufficiently large $n$ (specifically, $n$ greater than a tower of $2$'s of height roughly $10^{14}$). We present a proof of the Murty-Simon conjecture that works for all $n$. A proof of the $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ bound was originally found by AI; we simplified this proof and extended its ideas to get a proof of the full conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Sanjana Das, Jacob Fox

item.title: Bases for the Top-Degree Garsia-Haiman Module
item.description: arXiv:2610.39061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce two new monomial bases for the top $t$-degree component of the Garsia-Haiman module $V_\mu$ for every partition $\mu$. Both bases are indexed by column-strict standard fillings of shape $\mu$; the first has exponents governed by entrywise refinements of Haglund's combinatorial statistics for the modified Macdonald polynomials $\widetilde{H}_\mu(X;q,t)$. The second basis has exponents governed by an insertion algorithm of Bhattacharya-Ratheesh-Viswanath, and gives a basis realization of the ``fermionic formula" of the $m_{1^n}$-coefficient of the $q$-Whittaker polynomial. Our proof uses orbit harmonics, and is inspired by the original approach of Garsia and Haiman.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Chou

item.title: A lattice path model for Schubert and forest polynomials: positivity and combinatorial interpretations
item.description: arXiv:2610.39077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we give combinatorial interpretations of (i) the Graham-positive coefficients in the expansion of double Schur polynomials in the double fundamental quasisymmetric basis and (ii) the coefficients in the expansion of Grothendieck polynomials in the grove basis. To obtain these interpretations, we construct a common lattice path model for Schubert, Grothendieck, and double Schubert polynomials and their respective quasisymmetric counterparts: forest, grove, and double forest polynomials. The first interpretation answers a question of Bergeron, Gagnon, Nadeau, Spink, and Tewari asking for an explicit combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients. It also yields formulas for the equivariant degrees of the quasisymmetric Schubert cycles introduced by Bergeron, Gagnon, Spink, and Tewari. The specialization of the second interpretation recovers Nadeau and Tewari's Schubert-to-forest formula, expressed using the rightmost representatives of their Omega-equivalence classes.
item.dc:creator: Hojoon Lee

item.title: Weighted Tur\'an densities for hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bondy and Tuza generalized the Tur\'an problem for graphs to weighted graphs. Subsequently, F\"uredi and K\"undgen gave a solution in the case of cliques. We consider the weighted Tur\'an problem on hypergraphs and prove the first tight asymptotic result for 3-uniform hypergraphs. Specifically, we determine the weighted Tur\'an density of the generalized triangle $F_5 = \{abc, abd, cde\}$. We also prove weighted stability results and exact results. Many intriguing open problems remain, the most tantalizing of which is to determine the weighted Tur\'an density of the tetrahedron. Bounds for this density using flag algebras are presented.
item.dc:creator: David James, Bernard Lidick\'y, Dhruv Mubayi

item.title: Finding solutions with the Borsuk-Ulam theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.39092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many existence theorems in combinatorics and geometry reduce to the Borsuk-Ulam theorem or its generalizations. We study how these existence arguments can be turned into effective numerical methods when a simple example with a single known solution is available. The idea is to deform this example into the given problem and follow its solution during the deformation. We establish conditions under which this procedure reaches a solution and estimate the work needed for a prescribed accuracy. Mass partition problems illustrate the method for both continuous objects and finite point sets. In a fixed dimension, each step for point sets requires work proportional to the number of points; we give conditions under which the entire computation has this linear cost. We also study how changing the initial example can lead to other solutions and support a search for all of them.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R. Musin

item.title: Some results on intersecting families of triangulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.39116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kalai conjectured that the largest intersecting family of triangulations of an $n$-gon is the family consisting of all triangulations that contain a fixed ear (a chord of length $2$). What happens if we strengthen the intersecting condition to the condition that any two of the triangulations must intersect on a chord from a specified family of chords -- for example, what if any two triangulations intersect on a chord from some fixed point of the $n$-gon, or intersect on an ear? In this paper we verify Kalai's conjecture for families of triangulations in which any two intersect on a chord from some fixed point. We also show that any ear-intersecting family of triangulations has size at most $T_{n-1} +T_{n-3} = T_{n-1}(17/16 + o(1))$, where $T_{n-1}$ is the upper bound in Kalai's conjecture, namely the number of triangulations of an $(n-1)$-gon. This is based on an exact upper bound of $T_{n-1}$ for the size of a family of triangulations in which any two intersect on some ear from the set of all ears with one ear excluded.
item.dc:creator: Imre Leader, Ta Sheng Tan

item.title: Simplified dense model theorem for random discrete structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.39176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dense model theorems of Conlon and Gowers associate to each subset of a sparse random structure a dense set with approximately the same size and configuration counts after rescaling. This allows dense extremal results to be transferred to the random setting. Allen, B\"ottcher, Lada, and Mergoni Cecchelli recently generalised this approach and established a dense model theorem in an abstract hypergraph framework, with hypotheses that are readily verified in many applications. Both proofs use the separating hyperplane theorem to reduce the existence of dense models to an anti-correlation estimate. We give a simplified proof of a version of this theorem, inspired by the method of hypergraph containers. Our proof constructs dense models from small fingerprints, combining sampling with the R\"odl-Ruci\'nski deletion method.
item.dc:creator: Rajko Nenadov

item.title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.39228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an affirmative answer to the abstract group problem for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of L\'aszl\'o Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is universal and finitely universal, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given.
item.dc:creator: G. Militaru

item.title: Error terms for sums of two linear transformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.39235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal L_1,\mathcal L_2$ be irreducible and coprime linear transformations from $\mathbb{Z}^d$ to $\mathbb{Z}^d$. In this paper, we prove that, for every finite nonempty set $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d$, \[ |\mathcal L_1A+\mathcal L_2A| \ge \left(|\det\mathcal L_1|^{1/d}+|\det\mathcal L_2|^{1/d}\right)^d|A|-O\left(|A|^{1-1/d}\right). \] This confirms the conjecture of Conlon and Lim on the error term for two linear transformations.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Hui Yan

item.title: The Stable Tamari Lattice
item.description: arXiv:2610.39257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the stable Tamari lattice $\mathcal{ST}_n$, an infinite lattice on $\mathbb{N}^n$. The $r$-Tamari lattices on $r$-Dyck paths of height $n+1$ occur as a nested family of principal lower order ideals whose union is $\mathcal{ST}_n$. Partition-indexed principal lower order ideals recover the $\nu$-Tamari lattices associated with partition boundaries. We give an explicit coordinate description of the stable Tamari order in terms of interval vectors determined by the lower endpoint. These coordinates characterize comparability and covering relations, and their sum gives the maximum length of a chain between two comparable elements. Analogous coordinates determined by the upper endpoint give an explicit formula for the M\"obius function. We also construct an EL-labeling of every interval and show that every interval in $\mathcal{ST}_n$ is isomorphic to an interval in a classical Tamari lattice. We classify the possible $h$-vectors by Dyck paths and show that each $h$-vector fiber is parametrized by a unimodular basis of interval vectors. Combining this parametrization with the lower-endpoint coordinates, we obtain a finite rational formula for the multivariate generating function of the height generating functions of all principal lower order ideals. Under the $r$-Tamari realization, these height generating functions recover the interval generating functions of Bergeron and Pr\'eville-Ratelle.
item.dc:creator: Herman Chau, Spencer Daugherty, Sean Grate, Mark D. Haiman, Juan Carlos Mart\'inez Mori, Anna Pun

item.title: On two problems concerning the geodesic transversal number of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sharp upper and lower bounds on the geodesic transversal number of hypercubes. We also obtain a lower bound on the geodesic transversal number of Hamming graphs. As applications, we provide negative answers to two open problems concerning the geodesic transversal number.
item.dc:creator: Shi Chen, Xuanlong Ma, Tingzeng Wu

item.title: Linear hereditary quasirandomness
item.description: arXiv:2610.39317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conlon, Fox and Sudakov (\emph{Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.} \textbf{164} (2018), 385--399) conjectured that hereditary subgraph counts force quasirandomness with linear dependence on the counting error. We prove this for every graph containing an edge. Let \(H\) have \(r\) vertices and \(m\ge1\) edges, and fix \(p\in(0,1)\). If every subset \(S\) of an \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\) contains \(p^m|S|^r\pm\delta n^r\) labelled injective copies of \(H\), then \(\lvert e_G(A,B)-p|A||B|\rvert\le C_{H,p}\delta n^2\) for all \(A,B\subseteq V(G)\), where \(e_G(A,B)\) counts ordered adjacent pairs. The proof extracts averaged rooted counts and represents each nonlinear term by a linear map in one selected edge factor. Composing two such maps gives an edge substitution with a superlinear cut-norm bound. A separate star expansion gives stronger local estimates for triangle-free graphs. The linear order is best possible even when \(2e(G)/n^2=p+O(n^{-2})\).
item.dc:creator: Jun Yue

item.title: Diameter-two graphs whose mutual-visibility chromatic number equals their chromatic number
item.description: arXiv:2610.39430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A set $S$ of vertices of a graph $G$ is a mutual-visibility set if every pair of vertices of $S$ is joined by a shortest path whose internal vertices avoid $S$, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $\chi_\mu(G)$ is the least number of mutual-visibility sets into which $V(G)$ can be partitioned. Klav\v{z}ar, Kuziak, Valenzuela Tripodoro and Yero (2025) proved that $\chi_\mu(G)\le\chi(G)$ whenever $G$ has diameter two, observed that equality holds for complete bipartite graphs, and asked whether there are any other diameter-two graphs attaining equality. We answer this question in the affirmative. We construct a graph $G_{11}$ of order 11 and diameter two with $\chi_\mu(G_{11})=\chi(G_{11})=3$, and an infinite family of such graphs obtained from $G_{11}$ by replacing one vertex with pairwise non-adjacent copies of it.
item.dc:creator: Siddhesh Chaubal

item.title: Tur\'{a}n numbers for suspensions of bipartite 2-regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $R$, let $\widehat R:=K_1+R$ denote its suspension, obtained by adding a new vertex adjacent to every vertex of $R$. For every fixed nonempty bipartite $2$-regular graph $R$, we determine $\operatorname{ex}(n,\widehat{R})$ for all sufficiently large $n$ and characterize all extremal graphs. Three distinct cases arise, according as $R$ is $2C_6$, a disjoint union of copies of $C_4$, or neither of these. This extends the known exact Tur\'a results on odd wheels to suspensions of arbitrary bipartite 2-regular graphs.
item.dc:creator: Haoxing Wu, Junxue Zhang

item.title: A polynomial method over formal power series
item.description: arXiv:2610.39460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give new upper bounds on families of integer vectors with prescribed coordinate multiplicities and a forbidden scalar product. Our method uses coefficient functions over formal power series and recovers the Frankl--Wilson bound for binary vectors. For vectors in $\{-1,0,1\}^n$, we obtain an exponential improvement over the ordinary polynomial count in a wide range; in certain regimes, we determine the lower limit of the exponential base. We use the new bounds to make progress on several questions in combinatorial geometry. In particular, we improve the base of the exponent in Borsuk's partition problem: we construct finite subsets of $\mathbb R^N$ requiring at least $(1.37+o(1))^{\sqrt N}$ parts of smaller diameter for all sufficiently large $N$, and obtain a base of $1.3839$ along a subsequence of dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Artur Akhiiarov, Mikhail Koshelev, Andrey Kupavskii, Andrei Raigorodskii

item.title: The maximum number of triangles in regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the maximum number of triangles in $n$-vertex $k$-regular graphs and characterize all extremal graphs for all admissible orders when $k$ is odd and for an explicit range of orders when $k$ is even. For even $k$, we also give explicit lower and upper bounds for the remaining orders. As a consequence, we obtain a lower bound on the number of independent sets of size three in $k$-regular graphs and characterize all equality cases. Our exact results confirm the conjecture of Petingi and Rodr\'iguez and the triangle case of a conjecture of Cambie, de Joannis de Verclos and Kang for all odd $k$ and the specified orders when $k$ is even. Moreover, for every even $k\ge18$, we construct counterexamples to both conjectures and obtain a recursive characterization of all extremal graphs of order at least $Ck$, where $C$ is an absolute constant.
item.dc:creator: Ya-Hong Chen, Shi-Cai Gong, Changhong Lu, Zhuojie Tu, Long-Tu Yuan

item.title: Guaranteed indirect delivery in directed networks: The joint extremal function and explicit attaining constructions
item.description: arXiv:2610.39469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A messenger and a pursuer move alternately on a finite loopless directed graph, with complete information and waiting permitted. The messenger moves first and wins upon reaching a designated recipient, before interception there. We determine the maximum number $M(n,m)$ of ordered nonadjacent source--recipient pairs for which delivery is guaranteed against every initial pursuer position, among graphs with $n$ vertices and $m$ arcs. We give the exact value and an explicit attaining graph for every admissible pair $(n,m)$. For $n\ge12$, a piecewise formula describes sparse growth, the interval $2n\le m\le n(n-3)$ in which every missing pair can be guaranteed, a dense staircase, and the zero range above $n(n-2)$. Complete finite tables cover smaller orders. The proofs combine degree and support bounds, local strategy composition, protected routing, and constructions in the missing-arc graph. Finite exceptional cases use explicit strategy certificates and complete computational exclusions. Reproducible programs and certificates accompany the paper; a Lean development verifies the complete formula for $n\ge12$ and $m\ge24$, the claimed scores of prescribed constructions at every admissible pair, and further finite upper bounds. Its remaining obligations are stated separately.
item.dc:creator: Angel Ivanov Raychev

item.title: $e$-Positive caterpillars have maximum degree at most three
item.description: arXiv:2610.39481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dahlberg, She, and van Willigenburg conjectured that every $e$-positive tree has maximum degree at most three. We prove this conjecture for caterpillars. Our proof introduces a specialization--cone method: we evaluate chromatic symmetric functions under finite-support specializations that are nonnegative on the elementary symmetric functions, express the evaluations through transfer matrices, and certify negativity using finitely generated cones. Two specializations and three cones handle all caterpillars remaining after a connected-partition reduction, with no bound on the number or spacing of their trivalent vertices. The required cone inclusions and strict sign inequalities are certified by exact rational arithmetic. We also exhibit two infinite families of non-spider caterpillars of maximum degree four that admit connected partitions of every type, showing that Wolfgang's criterion alone leaves cases requiring further obstructions. Our result also reduces Li's criterion on $e$-positivity for caterpillars of maximum degree three to an explicit condition on the positions of trivalent vertices.
item.dc:creator: Davion Q. B. Tang, David G. L. Wang, Monica M. Y. Wang

item.title: Strongly explicit Ramanujan 2-lift towers via Hilbert modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.39485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Expander graphs have been central objects of study for over fifty years. Ramanujan graphs attain the asymptotically optimal nontrivial adjacency-eigenvalue threshold for infinite fixed-degree families. The original arithmetic constructions by Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak (1988) and Margulis (1988), and the iterative $2$-lift method of Bilu-Linial (2006) provide different approaches to Ramanujan graph constructions. Motivated by work on Mealy automata, we combine both approaches to give the following new arithmetic construction. For every prime $p\equiv 1\pmod {17}$, we construct a infinite tower of $(p+1)$-regular non-bipartite Ramanujan graphs on $2^n$ vertices, with label-preserving $2$-lifts between consecutive levels. These construction is strongly explicit: for fixed $p$, a neighbor or lift sign is computable in $O_p(n^3)$ bit operations. The construction uses fixed algebraic $2$-adic transformations, specified by finite data computable in preprocessing depending only on $p$. The main number-theoretic tool is Blasius's Ramanujan-Petersson theorem for Hilbert modular forms, applied through the Jacquet-Langlands correspondence to obtain the sharp bound $|\lambda|\leq2\sqrt p$ for every nontrivial adjacency eigenvalue of our $(p+1)$-regular graphs. The transformations preserve $2$-adic distance, which gives the binary covers and an explicit formula for their signings.
item.dc:creator: Olga Kharlampovich, Igor Pak, Alina Vdovina

item.title: On the Tur\'an Number of the Cartesian Product of Two Stars
item.description: arXiv:2610.39486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Tur\'an number of the Cartesian product of two stars, a family whose order of magnitude is known. For most pairs of star sizes, we determine the leading coefficient exactly. In the remaining congruence class, we give explicit lower and upper bounds for the coefficient at the leading scale. Our lower bounds use blowups of polarity graphs, and our upper bounds use structural estimates on neighbourhoods.
item.dc:creator: Quan Sun, Long-Tu Yuan

item.title: The complete existence spectrum of periodic complementary ternary pairs of weight nine
item.description: arXiv:2610.39501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For two sequences with entries $0,\pm1$, periodic complementarity means that their periodic autocorrelation functions sum to zero at every nonzero shift. We give necessary and sufficient conditions on the length for the existence of such pairs of total weight nine, where weight counts nonzero entries. The conditions decide existence at any prescribed length by divisibility tests. The main new result bounds the length of primitive pairs with two nonzero components. A pair is primitive if it cannot be shortened by removing uniformly inserted zeros after independent cyclic permutations. We prove primitive-length bounds of $64,48,64$ for weight distributions $(5,4),(6,3),(7,2)$. These bounds make the classification finite and prove that the earlier searches contain every required case. Exhaustive enumeration gives $91$ primitive sequence-equivalence classes. Including the five known circulant classes gives $96$ representatives from which every pair can be generated. The same catalogue gives class counts at every length. For constructing one pair, $33$ displayed seeds suffice. The results settle earlier conjectures on the weight distributions and decide exactly which orders admit the associated two-circulant weighing-matrix construction.
item.dc:creator: Stelios D. Georgiou, Stella Stylianou

item.title: Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers for 3-uniform tight hypergraph cycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.39578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C^{(3)}_n$ be the $3$-uniform tight cycle on $n$ vertices, that is, the $3$-uniform hypergraph on a cyclically ordered set of $n$ vertices whose edges are precisely the triples of consecutive vertices in the given cyclic order. We asymptotically determine the off-diagonal Ramsey numbers of $3$-uniform tight cycles. This is an off-diagonal analogue of a result of Haxell, {\L}uczak, Peng, R\"odl, Ruci\'nski and Skokan [Combin.\ Probab.\ Comput.\ 18 (2009), no.\ 1-2, 165--203] on the diagonal Ramsey numbers of $3$-uniform tight cycles.
item.dc:creator: Eng Keat Hng

item.title: The number of $C_4$-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Erd\H{o}s, Frankl and R\"odl showed that the number of graphs on $n$ vertices with no copy of a non-bipartite graph $H$ is $2^{(1+o(1))ex(n,H)}$, whereas Morris and Saxton showed that this fails for $C_6$. Answering a question of Erd\H{o}s, we prove that the number of $C_4$-free graphs on $n$ vertices is $2^{(1+o(1))ex(n,C_4)}$. The proof combines a modified hypergraph container method that treats pairs of vertices with large codegree separately, with a new bound on the number of matchings in a graph.
item.dc:creator: Tianchi Yang

item.title: Tiling circular $n$-boards with squares and (1,1)-fences
item.description: arXiv:2610.39599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the number of ways to tile a circular $n$-board (an annulus divided into $n$ curved unit square cells) with appropriately curved unit squares and curved (1,1)-fences is a Lucas number squared if $n$ is even and an odd-indexed Lucas number otherwise. A curved (1,1)-fence is composed of two curved unit squares separated by a gap in the shape of another curved unit square. This combinatorial interpretation of the Lucas numbers squared and the odd-indexed Lucas numbers allows us to obtain various identities concerning these sequences in a quick and lucid manner.
item.dc:creator: Michael A. Allen, Kenneth Edwards

item.title: Solutions to several problems on infinite sumset configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.39637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve a number of the problems collected by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson in their survey "Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond". Our main result is that in every countably infinite abelian group, every set of positive upper Banach density contains a sumset $B_1+\dots+B_k$ of $k$ infinite sets, for every $k$; the proof uses the Kronecker factor, but no higher-order Host-Kra structure theory, nilsystems of step greater than one, or nilspaces. We also answer, positively or negatively, questions on monochromatic sets $B+mB$, on sumsets in sets of logarithmic density, on polynomial sumset configurations, on sums of the form $B_{i_1}+\dots+B_{i_m}$ with $B_i$ drawn from a density family, on random sets, on ordered sumsets in shifted primes, on sums and products in $\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$, and on sumsets in abelian groups. Several of these answers concern the questions as literally stated, and two follow directly from known examples; in each case we say so and discuss the natural corrected question. Finally, answering a question of Kousek and Radi\'c, we show that the supremum of the lower Banach densities of sets $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B+B+t\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ and every $t\ge0$ (respectively $B+B\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B$) is $1/2$ (respectively $3/4$). The main theorem and most of the other results are formalized in Lean 4, with some published theorems entering as explicit hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Shisheng Li, Yong Su

item.title: On edge-ordered Ramsey numbers of hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an integer $h\geq2$, an edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $H^<$ is an $h$-uniform hypergraph with a linear ordering of its hyperedges. For an integer $q \geq 1$, the edge-ordered Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{edge}}(H^<;q)$ of $H^<$ is the smallest positive integer $N$ such that there exists an edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $G^<$ on $N$ vertices such that, for every $q$-coloring of the hyperedges of $G^<$, there is a monochromatic copy of $H^<$ in $G^<$ preserving the hyperedge order. In this note, we show that, for every edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $F^<$ on $n$ vertices with $m\geq1$ hyperedges, $R_{\mathrm{edge}}(F^<;q) \leq R_h(F;q)^{Cm^2}$ where $F$ is the underlying unordered hypergraph, $R_h(F;q)$ is its standard $q$-color Ramsey number, and $C=C(h,q)>0$ is a constant. For fixed $h\geq3$ and $q\geq2$, this shows that prescribing the hyperedge order does not require an increase in the tower height of the classical upper bound. It also settles a problem posed by Fox and Li (2020), and for $h=2$ gives the bound $2^{O(n^4\log n)}$, improving their bounds for every fixed $q \geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Martin Balko, Jelena Gli\v{s}i\'c

item.title: Minimum-degree thresholds beyond bounded colourability
item.description: arXiv:2610.39759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We survey recent developments on minimum-degree thresholds in extremal graph theory, with an emphasis on structural refinements of the chromatic-threshold problem. The chromatic threshold asks when a linear minimum-degree condition forces bounded chromatic number in an \(H\)-free graph; its complete classification shows a striking finite trichotomy. We discuss several stronger and related threshold notions in which bounded colourability is replaced by bounded \(H\)-free homomorphic images, bounded neighbourhood complexity via VC-dimension, exact blowup structure for maximal \(H\)-free graphs, and improved quantitative bounds in graph removal lemmas. In contrast with the rigidity of the chromatic threshold, these newer parameters exhibit richer behaviour, including separations from \(\delta_\chi(H)\), new exact values, accumulation points in fixed-chromatic spectra, positivity phenomena for 3-chromatic graphs, asymmetric variants, and failures of monotonicity.
item.dc:creator: Xinqi Huang, Hong Liu

item.title: EPPA for Reducts of the Random Graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.39760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that finite two-graphs have coherent EPPA and that neither graphs modulo global complementation nor two-graphs modulo global complementation have EPPA. This completes the classification of EPPA and coherent EPPA for the reducts of the random graph, answering a question and confirming a conjecture of Evans, Hubi\v{c}ka, Kone\v{c}n\'y and Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Brenner, Jan Hubi\v{c}ka, Mat\v{e}j Kone\v{c}n\'y

item.title: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.39870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We complete the determination of the minimum possible length of eight-dimensional binary self-orthogonal codes with given minimum distance. For dimension nine we give exact values and bounds for minimum distance at most $64$. By exploiting the geometric reformulation of linear codes as multisets of points, we fully redo the classification for dimension at most seven in a simplified and computer-free manner. As a by-product we prove the non-existence of $[93,9,44]_2$ codes and show several divisibility results for putative optimal nine-dimensional binary codes.
item.dc:creator: Sascha Kurz

item.title: The asymptotic number of zonotopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.39900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a sharp estimate for the asymptotic number of lattice zonotopes inscribed in [0, n] d as n tends to infinity. Our estimate refines the logarithmic equivalent established by B{\'a}r{\'a}ny, Bureaux, and Lund when the sum of the generators of the zonotope is prescribed. As we shall see, the exponential part of our estimate is a polynomial of degree d in n 1/(d+1) , plus a term involving the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Our analysis is based on a correspondence between power sums over primitive vectors (vectors with coprime coordinates) and Eulerian polynomials. We also analyse some combinatorial properties of lattice zonotopes. In particular, we compute the asymptotic mean and variance of the diameter of the graph of a random lattice zonotope inscribed in [0, n] d as n goes to infinity, and show that this diameter satisfies a central limit theorem.
item.dc:creator: Olivier Bodini (LAGA), Th\'eophile Buffi\`ere

item.title: Dense Minors from the Crux
item.description: arXiv:2610.39957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree $d>0$ and $C_\alpha(G)$ be the minimum order of a subgraph whose average degree is at least $\alpha d$ for any fixed $0<\alpha<1$. Then $G$ has a minor of average degree $\Omega(\sqrt{d\,C_\alpha(G)})$, which is asymptotically tight up to a constant factor. This reveals a unified mechanism underlying previous results on dense minors in locally sparse graphs.
item.dc:creator: Xia Wang, Donglei Yang

item.title: On the maximum interval index of a graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.39966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a connected graph P G on n vertices, the interval index is defined by Int(G) = {u,v} subset V(G) (|I(u, v)| - 1), where I(u, v) denotes the set of all vertices lying on a shortest u - v path. It was conjectured that, among all connected graphs on n vertices, the path Pn attains the maximum value of the interval index. In this paper we settle this conjecture, and we prove that the maximum is attained only for Pn, except for n = 4, when the cycle C4 attains the same value. We also prove that, for every n >= 31, the maximum interval index among graphs without pendant vertices equals (n^3 - n)/6 - 2(n - 4) and it is attained by a dumbbell graph, obtained by joining two 4-cycles by a path.
item.dc:creator: Martin Knor, Jelena Sedlar, Riste \v{s}krekovski

item.title: Complexity of finding color-avoiding connected components
item.description: arXiv:2610.39982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two vertices of a (not necessarily properly) arc-colored digraph are called arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected if, after the removal of the arcs of any at most $\ell$ colors, they remain strongly $k$-arc-connected. The arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components are maximal sets of vertices such that any two of those vertices belonging to the set are arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected in the graph. We investigate the problems of finding the arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components and the maximal arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected subgraphs of an arc-colored digraph. We also consider possible generalizations to $k$-vertex-connectivity and to vertex-colored digraphs. We show that despite the seemingly minor differences in definitions, the complexity of these problems varies significantly: some can be solved in polynomial time, while others are NP-hard. It also turns out that in some cases the problem is NP-hard when multiple colors can be assigned to each vertex, but the problem becomes polynomial-time solvable when each vertex is single-colored.
item.dc:creator: Panna T\'{i}mea Fekete, Roland Molontay, Kitti Varga

item.title: Submodular decompositions: a bounded-variation counterexample and an exact planar cut formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.40032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: B\'erczi, Geh\'er, Imolay, Lov\'asz, and Schwarcz (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40(2026), 308--335) asked whether every set function of bounded variation is a difference of two bounded submodular functions, and how to determine the optimum in a monotonic sum-decomposition of a planar graph cut function. In this paper, we answer both questions and obtain quantitative extensions. For the first question, we characterize the continuous profiles $f:[0,1]\to\R$ for which $A\mapsto f(m(A))$ is a bounded submodular difference on an atomless probability space. More precisely, we express the minimum oscillation of the subtracted component through the positive part of the distributional second derivative. We also characterize admissible discontinuous profiles and give an exact summability criterion for countable block functions. In particular, the first question has a negative answer even for increasing functions of variation one whose scalar profiles have log-Lipschitz derivatives and belong to every $C^{1,\alpha}$, $0<\alpha<1$. Turning to graph cuts, we prove that the optimum equals the total edge weight minus the maximum fractional triangle-packing weight for every nonnegative weighting if and only if the graph is $K_5$-free. Moreover, maximum packings parametrize the symmetrized optimal components, while on $K_4$-free graphs we describe all optimal components and characterize uniqueness. Consequently, the formula applies to weighted planar graphs and implies edge-weight monotonicity on $K_5$-free graphs. For rational weights, it also yields polynomial-time constructions.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Linlin Wang, Jun Yue

item.title: The bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three
item.description: arXiv:2610.40079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a rational analogue of an $\mathrm{A}_2^{(1)}$ Rogers--Ramanujan type identity discovered by Warnaar, we establish sum-like expressions for a bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three. These expressions provide the finishing touch towards conjectures of Warnaar and Kanade--Russell.
item.dc:creator: Shane Chern, Trieu Nguyen, Chanh Tran, Tanay Wakhare

item.title: On the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv Problem for $\mathbb{Z}_n^r$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv problem is a classical extremal problem in discrete geometry. We prove that, for all positive integers $n$ and $r$, every sequence of $4^r n$ lattice points in $\mathbb{Z}^r$ contains $n$ points whose centroid is again a lattice point.
item.dc:creator: Dongchun Han, Hanbin Zhang

item.title: Full immersions in Eulerian group-labeled graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An immersion of a graph H in a graph G is full if the immersion uses every edge of G. We give a structure theorem for group-labeled Eulerian graphs excluding a fixed group-labeled graph as a full immersion.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis Eleftheriadis, Rose McCarty, Caleb McFarland, Evangelos Protopapas, Paul Wollan

item.title: A lifted entropy splitting lemma and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.40145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a matrix lifting of the entropy-splitting theorem of Csisz\'ar, K\"orner, Lov\'asz, Marton, and Simonyi, and show several applications. We use it to prove the Cartesian-product inequality conjectured by Sinjorgo and Sotirov for the generalized Lov\'asz theta number, and we also answer the saturation and convexification questions of Carli Silva, Coutinho, Oliveira, and Tun\c{c}el on the same theme. For the strong Hoffman bound, we answer a question of Wocjan, Elphick, and Darbari concerning orthogonal rank, and show that optimization over matrix weights gives exactly the ceiling of the theta number of the complement. Finally, we extend the lifting to diagonally invariant cones of positive semidefinite matrices, giving a proof of a conjecture by Kuryatnikova, Sotirov, and Vera, and giving a short proof, for all graphs, of a theta-based weakening of Fajtlowicz's graph-energy conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Coutinho, Luis Higino

item.title: On separators in $K_t$-minor-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This manuscript presents a proof of the Alon--Seymour--Thomas conjecture developed under the author's guidance using ChatGPT 6pro. The author has checked every formula and theorem by hand and used Codex to assist with writing. GPT 6.1 Sol (Max) was also used to check the proof repeatedly and to generate numerous examples for verification. More precisely, for every integer $h\geq3$, every $n$-vertex $K_h$-minor-free graph has a vertex set of size at most $\min{n,21h\sqrt n}$ whose deletion leaves every component with at most $2n/3$ vertices.
item.dc:creator: Xinheng Lin

item.title: The Borodin--Kostochka Conjecture for Two Classes of Diamond-Free Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Borodin--Kostochka conjecture for $(\mathrm{diamond},L_4)$-free graphs and $(\mathrm{diamond},K_5^+)$-free graphs, where $L_4$ is obtained from $K_4$ by attaching a path of length two to one clique vertex, and $K_5^+$ is obtained from $K_5$ by adding a vertex adjacent to exactly one clique vertex. The proof uses structural properties of maximum cliques in diamond-free vertex-critical graphs with $\chi=\Delta$.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Fiujlaali

item.title: Computer-Assisted Results for \(n\)-Sided Non-Transitive Dice Taking Face Values in \([n]\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.40321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider non-transitivity among dice with \(n\) sides restricted to taking face values in the set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). We give a computer-assisted proof that \(n=6\) is the smallest \(n\ge3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage. For \(n=6\), we identify the two unique non-transitive cycles of length \(6\). We present computational evidence supporting a conjecture that \(n=6\) is the largest \(n\ge3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage.
item.dc:creator: Terry Easlick

item.title: A p-adic Valuation Calculus for Permutations with Restricted Cycle Lengths
item.description: arXiv:2610.40342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let a_A(n) be the number of permutations of {1,...,n} all of whose cycle lengths lie in a set A. We develop a valuation calculus for these numbers. Mobius inversion writes the exponential generating function as an Euler product, and at a prime p the factors with non-p-integral exponents, the blocks, determine a finite knapsack problem. Its optimal value gives a lower bound for v_p(a_A(n)), and the bound is attained exactly when one residue modulo p, the sum of the terms of the optimal choices, does not vanish. For a fixed set A and prime p the bounds and residues for all n <= N cost O(N^2) operations. When one block is strictly the most efficient, the valuation inside each residue class is that of a locally analytic p-adic function. We use the calculus to determine the 2-adic and 3-adic valuations for cycle lengths at most 3, 4 and 5, to prove the divisibility conjectures recorded in A378495, A079128, A193437 and A193438 and the 3-adic statements recorded in A057693 and A070945, and to treat 99 OEIS sequences in all. We also prove sharp divisibility and gcd theorems, show that at n = 111 the gcd of the counts over all sets of excluded cycle lengths containing {1,2,3} is one third of the gcd over the sets {1,2,3,k}, and determine eventual divisibility and tail gcds modulo composite integers. Part of the paper is formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Ahaan Kallat

item.title: Johnson optimality and uniqueness for distance ratio $1:\sqrt{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a two-distance set in $\mathbb R^d$ with distance ratio $1:\sqrt{2}$ has at most $d(d+1)/2$ points for every $d\ge9$. Equality in full affine dimension characterizes the Johnson construction; for $d\ge10$, the full-dimensional condition is automatic. The proof separates configurations according to the connectivity of the short-distance graph. The connected case uses root lattices and intersection theorems, while the disconnected case uses an orthogonal decomposition into component direction spaces and the span of their center differences. We also prove a relative bound for Euclidean two-distance sets and show that equality forces sphericity. Together with the Larman--Rogers--Seidel theorem, these results give maximum cardinality $d(d+1)/2$ for $9\le d\le21$ and $275$ for $d=22$, without exhaustive enumeration.
item.dc:creator: Bryan Bu, Chin-Yen Lee, Yu-Hang Sheng, Meng-Tsung Tsai, Hyunjun Yi, Wei-Hsuan Yu

item.title: The maximum degree of Nosal graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph $G$ with $m$ edges is a Nosal graph if its spectral radius $\lambda(G)$ exceeds $\sqrt m$. At the threshold $\lambda(G)=\sqrt m$, the star $K_{1,m}$ shows that one vertex can be incident with all $m$ edges. In contrast, Li, Liu and Zhang [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 179 (2026)] proved that every Nosal graph $G$ with sufficiently many edges satisfies $\Delta(G)\le\frac12m+m^{0.99}$, where the constant $\frac12$ is best possible. In this paper, we prove that every Nosal graph $G$ with spectral radius $\lambda$ satisfies $\Delta(G)<m-\frac12(\lambda-1)(\lambda-2)$, and hence $\Delta(G)<\frac12m+\frac32\sqrt m-1$. Both bounds are sharp up to an additive constant less than $\frac12$: for every $r\ge3$, the complete graph $K_r$ with $\frac12(r^2+r-2)$ pendant vertices attached to one vertex is a Nosal graph with $r^2-1$ edges whose maximum degree lies within $\frac12$ of both bounds. Consequently, the largest maximum degree of a Nosal graph with $r^2-1$ edges is exactly $\frac12(r^2+3r-4)$. The first bound cannot be improved by any positive additive constant: its gap on these graphs is less than $\frac{4}{r+5}$ and tends to zero as $r\to \infty$.
item.dc:creator: Yongtao Li

item.title: Thin ends and topological spanning trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.40458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Halin conjectured in 1964 that every connected graph has an end-faithful spanning tree. He proved this for countable graphs, but in the early 1990s Seymour and Thomas and, independently, Thomassen found uncountable counterexamples. Both are infinitely connected and hence one-ended, and their unique end has uncountable degree (i.e.\ contains uncountably many pairwise disjoint rays). Several authors have since asked how much of the conjecture survives. Diestel asked in 1992 whether a graph has an end-faithful spanning tree as soon as all its one-ended connected subgraphs have one; by a theorem of Polat, this would give end-faithful spanning trees in all connected graphs whose ends have countable degree. Diestel and K\"uhn introduced topological spanning trees, a topological variant of end-faithful spanning trees that exists in every one-ended connected graph, and asked in 2004 whether every connected graph has one. And Carmesin asked in 2019 whether every graph has a spanning tree that is end-faithful at least for its thin ends, the ends of finite degree. We answer all three questions in the negative. We show that the uncountably chromatic graph from an earlier note of ours on a problem of Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal has only ends of countable degree, each dominated by only countably many vertices, yet it has neither an end-faithful nor a topological spanning tree. A refinement of this graph moreover has no spanning tree that contains a ray from every end of degree~1.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Bowler, Max Pitz

item.title: Average pairwise Hamming distance of a subset in a hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2610.40486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we prove that for a subset $\mathcal{F}$ of $\{0,1\}^n$ of density $\frac{1}{8}$, its average pairwise Hamming distance is at least $\frac{n-3}{2}$, with equality attained only by $(n-3)$-dimensional subcubes. This answers a question of Lei Yu, and solves an important open case of a more general question posed by Ahlswede and Katona in 1977.
item.dc:creator: Yijia Fang, Hao Huang

item.title: Real-rooted Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown posets and wheel and whirl matroids
