item.description: arXiv:2610.40496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown order polytopes are real-rooted, settling a conjecture of Lundstr\"om and Saud Maia Leite. For each integer $r\ge3$, the crown order polytope on $2r$ elements and the rank-$r$ whirl base polytope have the same $h^*$-polynomial. The $h^*$-polynomials of the rank-$r$ wheel and whirl base polytopes, as well as every convex combination of the two, have $2r-2$ distinct negative roots. Their coefficient sequences are positive, unimodal, and strictly ultra log-concave of order $2r-2$.
item.dc:creator: Ying Cao, Houshan Fu

item.title: Supersaturation: Cliques and Positive Square Energy
item.description: arXiv:2610.40570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n$ and let $k_r$ denote the number of unlabeled copies of $K_r$ in $G$. Let $s^+$ denote the sum of the squares of the positive adjacency eigenvalues of $G$. For every fixed integer $r\geq2$, we prove that, as $n \to \infty$ \[ \sqrt{s^+}>\left(1-\frac1r\right)n \quad\Longrightarrow\quad k_{r+1}\geq \left(\frac1{r^{r-1}}-o_r(1)\right)n^{r-1}. \] The coefficient $r^{-(r-1)}$ is asymptotically best possible; in particular, the triangle case gives $k_3\geq n/2-o(n)$. The proof combines positive square energy stability, the clique removal lemma, and a sharp clique count around a maximum $r$-cut. The triangle case requires an additional block-matrix argument.
item.dc:creator: Abhay Jayarajan, M. Rajesh Kannan, Shivaramakrishna Pragada

item.title: The Number of Tropical Order Types and Coherent Matching Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.40622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate counting problems for discrete (geometric) structures in tropical settings, motivated by the comparison of the expressivity of linear programs and mean-payoff games. First, we give an upper bound on the number of coherent matching fields of type $(n,r)$ and a lower bound on the number of combinatorial types of $n$-hyperplane sequences in the max-plus tropical space of dimension $r-1$. These structures are closely related, and our bounds establish that as $n \to \infty$, for every fixed $r$ their number equals $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$. This in turn implies that the number of regular triangulations of the products of simplices $\Delta^{n-1}\times\Delta^{r-1}$ is also $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$, thereby answering a question of Santos. Second, we obtain that the number of labeled order types over the reals and over the signed tropical numbers coincide at first order, establishing a comparison of the expressivity of mean-payoff games and linear programs as measured by labeled order types. Last, the subclass of mean-payoff games known as parity games arise from linear programs by a ``double tropicalization.'' We show that the number of labeled order types obtained after this double tropicalization collapses.
item.dc:creator: Xavier Allamigeon, Yiyuan Chen, St\'ephane Gaubert, Xavier Goaoc

item.title: Approximation Algorithms for Matroid-Intersection Coloring with Applications to Rota's Basis Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2604.03735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study algorithmic matroid intersection coloring. Given $k$ matroids on a common ground set $U$ of $n$ elements, the goal is to partition $U$ into the fewest number of color classes, where each color class is independent in all matroids. It is known that $2\chi_{\max}$ colors suffice to color the intersection of two matroids, $(2k-1)\chi_{\max}$ colors suffice for general $k$, where $\chi_{\max}$ is the maximum chromatic number of the individual matroids. However, these results are non-constructive, leveraging techniques such as topological Hall's theorem and Sperner's Lemma. We provide the first polynomial-time algorithms to color two or more general matroids where the approximation ratio depends only on $k$ and, in particular, is independent of $n$. For two matroids, we constructively match the $2\chi_{\max}$ existential bound, yielding a 2-approximation for the Matroid Intersection Coloring problem. For $k$ matroids we achieve a $(k^2-k)\chi_{\max}$ coloring, which is the first $O(1)$-approximation for constant $k$. Our approach introduces a novel matroidal structure we call a \emph{flexible decomposition}. We use this to formally reduce general matroid intersection coloring to graph coloring while avoiding the limitations of partition reduction techniques, and without relying on non-constructive topological machinery. Furthermore, we give a \emph{fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme} (FPRAS) for coloring the intersection of two matroids when $\chi_{\max}$ is large. This yields the first polynomial-time constructive algorithm for an asymptotic variant of Rota's Basis Conjecture. This constructivizes Montgomery and Sauermann's recent asymptotic breakthrough and generalizes it to arbitrary matroids.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Arndt, Benjamin Moseley, Kirk Pruhs, Chaitanya Swamy, Michael Zlatin

item.title: Bayesian Probing on Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2606.09729v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a stochastic probing problem with correlated items. In our model, which we call Bayesian Probing, the correlations are modeled by an underlying graph $G$. Each vertex is independently active with a known probability. Each item corresponds to an edge in the graph. Probing an edge has some cost, gives some reward if both endpoints are active, and also reveals the state of its endpoints. Hence a probe induces a Bayesian update on the remaining edges. The goal is to adaptively probe items/edges subject to a knapsack constraint to maximize the expected total reward obtained from the probed edges. Bayesian Probing generalizes stochastic knapsack and stochastic probing by allowing correlations between items. Moreover, it gives a tractable model for the Bayesian Active Search problem, a popular problem considered in the machine learning community. In Bayesian Active Search, the goal is to find items in a particular class by adaptively probing at most, say $k$, items. Given a prior distribution over items, we want to compute a Bayesian policy to maximize the number of such items found. For this general problem with arbitrary priors, there are strong lower bounds on efficiently computing good policies. In this paper, we design efficient approximation algorithms for Bayesian Probing. These results give the first efficient approximation algorithms for Bayesian Active Search, for a class of practically-relevant prior distributions.
item.dc:creator: Anupam Gupta, Benjamin Moseley, Rudy Zhou

item.title: Matroid Contention Resolution with Concentration
item.description: arXiv:2607.09268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Contention resolution schemes (CRS) are a fundamental and widely applied tool for rounding fractional solutions subject to combinatorial constraints. However, the known analyses of CRS generally only guarantee lower bounds on the expected value and concentration on the upper tail, but no concentration on the lower tail. Thus, CRS are generally not applicable to problems that contain covering constraints, since certifying a covering constraint holds requires a lower tail bound. Our main contribution is to derive lower tail bounds for the output of a particular contention resolution scheme, the random-order CRS of Adamczyk and W{\l}odarczyk, which we call AW. We show that every linear function of the rounded solution attains a constant fraction of its expectation with a failure probability that is dimension-free, depending only on the expected value and on the number of matroids, but not on the size of the ground set. Our analysis is driven by a new property we call \emph{strong $\lambda$-boundedness}, which strengthens the known $\lambda$-boundedness of AW by providing two-sided control on how rounding propagates between elements. We then introduce a random process capturing AW, a \emph{sequential selection process}, that may be of independent interest. We prove lower tail bounds for any strongly $\lambda$-bounded sequential selection process. To demonstrate the applicability of our new tail bounds, we apply them to two problems involving covering constraints. The first result is an $O(k \log k)$-approximation for $k$-matroid intersection coloring (improving the prior $O(k^2)$) when the chromatic number of at least one matroid is $\Omega(k^3 \log n)$, where $n$ is the number of elements. The second is the first bicriteria approximation algorithm for monotone submodular maximization under $k$ matroid constraints together with packing and covering constraints.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Arndt, Benjamin Moseley, Kirk Pruhs, Michael Zlatin

item.title: Explicit matrix hitting points for noncommutative algebraic branching programs
item.description: arXiv:2610.37677v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-resource black-box identity test for noncommutative algebraic branching programs (ABPs), using ordinary matrix evaluations of the output polynomial. Given an alphabet of size $m\ge1$ and an ABP vertex bound $S\ge1$, we construct one fixed tuple of integer matrices of order $R=(m+2)d(d+1)/2$, where $d=(m+2)S$, with entry bit length $O(d\log(d+1))$. Every nonzero polynomial computed by an ABP with at most $S$ vertices has a nonzero evaluation at this tuple. The construction accesses neither the hidden ABP nor its intermediate gates. A rectangular variant improves the order to $O(m^{3/2}S^2)$. Matrix order, description length, and all returned entries are counted; the total resources are polynomial. The result holds in characteristic zero and in characteristic $p>\binom d2$. The main ingredient is a fixed polynomial frame spanning the joint cyclic module of every matrix tuple from every prescribed vector. A compensating block makes a tagged encoding nilpotent of index at most three, while preserving the original cyclic module. A differential exterior-vector argument then gives a single triangular recurrence with polynomially many outputs. Its shared left-linear circuit is converted into actual integer query matrices by coefficient duality. Two-sided pairing further gives deterministic nonadaptive reconstruction of an equivalent ABP from polynomially many output-only matrix queries. The same frame gives polynomial-cardinality explicit trace separators for simultaneous-conjugation orbit closures, and a fixed nilpotent substitution for bounded-dimensional recognizable series. The latter also tests rational formulas whose given syntax is defined at the scalar origin. We provide complete proofs, construction costs, and exact implementation checks.
item.dc:creator: Zhipeng Lu

item.title: Invariance in half-space last passage percolation and directed polymers
item.description: arXiv:2610.37694v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove various invariance properties for half-space geometric and exponential last passage percolation and the half-space log-gamma polymer, analogous to the full-space invariances proved by Dauvergne. We use the RSK and geometric RSK correspondences to establish a conditional distributional identity between the half-space models and the corresponding full-space models, which allows us to directly transfer the invariance results in the full space to the half space.
item.dc:creator: Yunhao Lou

item.title: The View-Obstruction Problem for Spheres in Dimensions Six and Seven
item.description: arXiv:2610.37711v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Place closed Euclidean balls of radius r at the points of (1/2, 1/2, ..., 1/2) + Z^n. The view-obstruction problem for spheres asks for the least r such that every ray from the origin into the open positive orthant meets a ball. Equivalently, it asks for D_n = sup_v min_{t in R} sum_i ||t v_i - 1/2||{Z}^2 over positive integer vectors v, where ||x||{Z} denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer. The values for n <= 5 are classical. We prove D_6 = 107/312, attained only by permutations of (12, 9, 7, 5, 3, 2), and D_7 = 73/180, attained only by permutations of (11, 10, 8, 7, 4, 3, 1). The proof reduces the supremum to a finite search. The key facts are an exact lower bound d_n(v) >= delta^2_U for every rational subspace U perpendicular to v, a matching fiber upper bound, and Banaszczyk's transference theorem, applied along the Korkine-Zolotarev flag of the dual lattice v^perpendicular intersection Z^n. The search is quotiented by signed coordinate permutations and carried out entirely in exact rational arithmetic. It terminates with a certificate: no node of the search is left unresolved, and every surviving candidate is evaluated exactly. The method also recovers the known values for n = 3, 4, 5.
item.dc:creator: Vineet Kahlon

item.title: Local-to-Global Theorems Based on Cones with Applications to Graph Coloring
item.description: arXiv:2610.37721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local-to-Global theorems are a cornerstone of many of recent developments in theoretical computer science from coding theory and PCPs all the way to analyzing mixing time of Markov chains. Building on trickledown theorems on simplicial complexes, several techniques have been established to obtain tighter local-to-global theorems to analyze the spectral gap of the Glauber dynamics, namely matrix trickledown, ${\mathcal C}$-Lorentzian polynomials and more recently Bochner type inequalities. In this paper, we adopt non-local local-to-global/Bochner type inequalities on "cones", corresponding to the local neighborhood of a given vertex, to show that the Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time to sample proper colorings of maximum degree $\Delta$ graphs as long as $q\geq 1.7408\Delta$.
item.dc:creator: Anqi Li, Shayan Oveis Gharan

item.title: Ternary analogs of dendriform algebras and quadri-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.37848v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct ternary analogs of dendriform algebras and quadri-algebras, generalizing the well-known binary case. These new structures are defined in terms of nonsymmetric operads. We construct these new operads using ternary operations defined in terms of ternary Rota-Baxter operators. The relations defining these operads lie in the quadratic subspace of the kernel of a rewriting morphism from a free operad to the operad generated by one associative ternary operation and one (or two commuting) unary operators satisfying the ternary Rota-Baxter relation(s). We use computational algebra to compute a basis for the quadratic component of the kernel and thereby obtain the quadratic relations which define these new operads. In the dendriform case, we obtain 3 operations satisfying 10 relations. In the quadri-algebra case, we obtain 9 operations satisfying 50 relations. The latter computations combine modular and rational arithmetic, but we are able to provide certificates of the results which can be verified in characteristic 0.
item.dc:creator: Yu Hin (Gary), Au, Murray R. Bremner

item.title: Finite-Sample Optimal Conformal Prediction Sets under Covariate Shift
item.description: arXiv:2610.37866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study conformal prediction under covariate shift with a known covariate density ratio, seeking prediction sets with minimum expected length under the target distribution. For every calibration sample size, we prove that the rule combining the inverse conditional-density score with randomized weighted conformal calibration minimizes this expected length among all rules valid over the full weighted-exchangeability class. We approximate the oracle using quantile and kernel histograms, including forest-weighted estimators, and select estimators and tuning parameters by resampling to estimate calibrated target length. On a bounded response domain, we bound excess length linearly in $L^1$ density error at fixed calibration size, without requiring a uniform positive lower bound on the true density. We also bound selection-pool and resampling errors. Under explicit growth conditions, the selected procedure approaches the same oracle while the calibration size remains fixed. Experiments on 36 known-density configurations and four public regression datasets compare coverage, prediction-set length, and runtime with existing methods. In targeted low-coverage and strong-shift comparisons, inverse-density selection yields shorter mean sets in most cases and lower mean runtime than the evaluated weighted baselines, with some differences in achieved coverage.
item.dc:creator: Zhongyang Li

item.title: Enumeration Complexity of Permutation Classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.37940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study classes of permutations that are defined by avoidance of forbidden patterns. For each fixed finite set $B$ of forbidden patterns, we study the \emph{avoider enumeration problem}: given an integer $n$, output all $B$-avoiding permutations of length $n$. Avoider enumeration is output-polynomial for every fixed $B$. However, our main notion of efficiency is polynomial delay. We use the insert-maximum tree as a search tree, in which permutations are built by repeatedly inserting a new maximum while preserving pattern avoidance. This leads to the \emph{insert-maximum extension problem}, which asks if a given permutation has an avoiding descendant at a specified depth. An algorithm for this problem can prune branches that cannot reach the target length. Hence, if this problem is in P, we obtain polynomial-delay enumeration. To investigate this problem, we introduce and study \emph{pockets}, the maximal finite subtrees of the insert-maximum tree. For fixed $B$, if there is a polynomial $p$ such that every pocket rooted at $\rho$ has at most $p(|\rho|)$ nodes, then the extension problem is solvable in polynomial time and enumeration has polynomial delay. In particular, a bound on pocket depth depending only on $B$ suffices. We prove such a bound if the class is well-quasi-ordered, has a regular insertion encoding, or if $B$ omits one of the three maximum-position types: leftmost, interior, or rightmost. We also prove that extension is in NP for every fixed $B$, even with binary-encoded target depth. On the negative side, we construct a fixed set of $55$ forbidden patterns for which extension is NP-complete. Consequently, enumerating valid extensions from a given starting permutation cannot have polynomial delay unless P=NP. This also answers a question of Hanika by showing that the forbidden permutation constraint satisfaction problem can be NP-complete for a fixed forbidden set.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Bodirsky, Mohamed Elsheikh

item.title: Diagrams for Roots and Quiver Representations in the context of the Gabriel-Kac Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.37969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using the data of the Dynkin diagrams, we build graphical calculi for representing the positive roots of Kac-Moody algebras and the representations of quivers. Once developed, we use these to analyze the asymptotic size of the root and representation spaces, and discuss how this relates to the Gabriel-Kac theorem, the correspondence between these two structures. We give a refinement of this correspondence in terms of the trichotomy of growth rates for Kac-Moody algebras depending on if they are of finite, affine, or indefinite type, which is done in terms of what we call ``tree like" representations.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Canel

item.title: Asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ of stable pointed curves and the all-light Hassett spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0|n}$, for fixed genus $g\ge1$ as the number of markings tends to infinity. We prove central limit theorems for the full Betti distributions, whose variances grow linearly in $n$ with leading coefficients independent of the genus. For the normalized even Betti numbers, we establish refined local limit theorems with estimates uniform in degree. These local estimates yield asymptotic formulas for individual even Betti numbers and determine the sharp central ultra-log-concavity thresholds $\frac{3(e-2)}{2(3-e)}$ and $3$, respectively. For $g\ge2$, the off-diagonal Hodge components form proportions of exact orders $n^{-1/2}$ and $n^{-1}$ of the total cohomology of the two spaces, respectively. The conditional distributions of the Hodge difference $p-q$ given $p\ne q$ converge, for both spaces, to a single discrete law independent of the genus. We also prove that tautological classes account for all but a proportion of exact order $n^{-1}$ of the even cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$. The tautological degree distribution converges to the standard Gaussian under the centering and scaling of the ambient even Betti distribution. An explicit asymptotic formula for the ratio of the ordinary Euler characteristics of the light and heavy spaces answers a question of Kannan, Serpente and Yun. The proofs combine the heavy/light substitution with a stratification of the light spaces by stable cores, singularity analysis of Hodge generating functions, and refined Fourier estimates exploiting Poincar\'e duality.
item.dc:creator: Jinwon Choi, Young-Hoon Kiem

item.title: Sharp Bounds on Torsional Rigidity of Metric Graphs with Signed Delta-Vertex Strengths
item.description: arXiv:2610.38330v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study torsional rigidity on finite compact connected metric graphs with real \(\delta\)-vertex strengths in the regime of strictly positive torsion. For a fixed total length \(L>0\), let \(I_+\) be the sum of the positive strengths and \(I_-\) the sum of the magnitudes of the negative strengths, with \(I_+>I_-\). We determine the sharp infimum and the exact threshold for a finite universal supremum. The supremum is finite precisely when \(I_-<I_+/(1+LI_+)\). In this regime, an interval with strengths \(I_+\) and \(-I_-\) at opposite endpoints attains the sharp Saint--Venant bound. At and beyond the threshold, torsional rigidity is unbounded even among three-vertex paths with the same data and strictly positive torsion. The sharp infimum is \(L^2/(I_+-I_-)\) throughout the range \(I_+>I_-\ge0\). It is not attained by any finite graph and is approached by graphs with two vertices joined by increasingly many parallel edges of equal length, preserving both strength totals separately. A vertex-matrix formulation and explicit path examples clarify the relation between strength placement, spectral positivity, and solvability.
item.dc:creator: Sedef \"Ozcan

item.title: Dimension-free exponential entropy quotients over $\mathbb{F}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a random vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^m$, and let $X'$ be an independent copy. We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a subspace $G$ with $\dim G\le 2^{320(1+\varepsilon)/\varepsilon}H(X)$ such that $H(q_GX)\le(1+\varepsilon)(H(q_GX+q_GX')-H(q_GX))$. In particular, the quotient entropy is at most $(1+\varepsilon)(H(X+X')-H(X))$. The coefficient is independent of the ambient dimension, and its exponential order in $1/\varepsilon$ is necessary. The structural result is a logarithmic rigidity estimate for finite weighted families of laws with averaged subspace entropy sparsity. A common variational quotient controls both a family and its convolution family without decreasing the original family's normalized mean entropy defect. Posterior families preserve averaged sparsity, and a fresh-index argument combines a local-to-global estimate with the entropic Marton theorem to increase the defect ratio at a fixed multiplicative sparsity cost. We also obtain two-input almost-additivity and concentration of moderate-doubling sets on subspace cosets at the same exponential scale. The constants are not optimized.
item.dc:creator: Josiah Park

item.title: Equivalence of freeness and higher order freeness of hyperplane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2610.38550v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using vector bundle theory, we prove that an essential hyperplane arrangement in an $\ell$-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic zero is free if and only if its module of logarithmic derivations of order $p$ is free for some $1\le p\le\ell-1$. The same statement holds for multiarrangements.
item.dc:creator: Takuro Abe

item.title: Estimating the number of nodes and paths in a DAG by following a random path
item.description: arXiv:2610.38586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate a simple method to compute an unbiased estimate of the number of nodes of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) by following a random directed path. This method is due to Leonard Pitt from 1987, and it generalizes a method of D. E. Knuth from the 1960s for estimating the size of a rooted tree. A slight variation makes it possible to estimate the number of source-sink paths. We extend the algorithm to use many "agents" that walk cooperatively through the graph. This extension unifies and generalizes several methods that have been proposed for approximately counting the nodes of a tree.
item.dc:creator: G\"unter Rote

item.title: Regularity of Symbolic Powers of Polymatroidal Ideals and Supermodular Prime Intersections
item.description: arXiv:2610.38655v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $S=\mathbb{K}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $\mathbb{K}$. For a polymatroidal ideal $I\subseteq S$ generated in degree $d$, we prove $$\omega(I^{(s)})=\operatorname{reg} I^{(s)}=\operatorname{reg} I^s=sd\qquad(s\ge1),$$ where symbolic powers use all associated primes and $\omega$ denotes the largest degree of a minimal generator. Thus every symbolic power has a degree resolution. The argument uses a regularity bound for supermodular prime intersections, obtained from Takayama's formula and a homological estimate for noncover complexes. For every nonzero proper squarefree monomial ideal $L$, we also show $\operatorname{reg} L^{(s)}\le s\min\{m,\lambda(L)-\operatorname{ht}L+1\}$, where $m$ counts the minimal primes and $\lambda(L)$ is the support size, and obtain equality for skeleton and pure skeleton ideals. Finally, for every $d\ge3$, we construct a simple graphic matroid whose basis ideal is generated in degree $d$ and has a second symbolic power that is not componentwise linear.
item.dc:creator: Chwas Ahmed, Mohammed Rafiq Namiq

item.title: Upper Bounds for CSP Non-redundancy via Locally Decodable Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.38664v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the study of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs), the non-redundancy of a relation measures the maximum number of clauses in a CSP instance which can be logically independent. In the last few years, CSP non-redundancy has found a number of applications including in query complexity, sparsification, kernelization and streaming. In this paper, we present a novel technique for upper-bounding the non-redundancy of some relations using locally decodable codes (LDCs) and locally correctable codes (LCCs). More precisely, known limitations on the structure of 2-query LDCs and LCCs can be translated into limitations on the size of certain non-redundant CSP instances. This technique builds on a technique used by Brakensiek and Guruswami [STOC 2025] to bound non-redundancy via techniques from matching vector codes. Using LDCs and LCCs, we give improved upper bounds on non-redundancy of the BCK predicate pioneered by Bessiere, Carbonnel, and Katsirelos [AAAI 2020] as well as its well-studied Boolean variant. We also give the first example of a Boolean predicate whose non-redundancy is provably not of the form $n^{k\pm o(1)}$ for some positive integer $k$.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Brakensiek, David Conlon, Venkatesan Guruswami, Xiaoyu He, Jiaxi Nie, Maya Sankar, Hung-Hsun Hans Yu

item.title: All-even sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Call a finite nonempty point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ all-even if for every direction $\ell \in \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, the number of hyperplanes perpendicular to $\ell$ that intersect $S$ is even. In 2026, Francisco Santos presented a question of Juan Benigno Seoane-Sep\'ulveda on the existence of all-even sets in dimensions $3$ and higher, together with examples of such sets in dimension $2$. Call a set $S\in\mathbb{R}^d$ line-all-even if for every direction $\ell \in \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ the number of lines parallel to $\ell$ that intersect $S$ is even. As Santos pointed out, every all-even set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is line-all-even. We conjecture that there exist no line-all-even sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that affinely span $\mathbb{R}^3$ We show that our conjecture is equivalent to the statement that every planar all-even set satisfies a certain property, which we call height-rigidity. This property has a natural interpretation in linear algebra terms. Furthermore, we present a hierarchy of properties of planar point sets that imply height-rigidity. We construct several all-even sets in the plane, including some infinite families, and show that all the sets we constructed are height-rigid. In addition, we prove that every all-even set in the plane that can be covered by six or fewer parallel lines is height-rigid.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Kalmanovich, Gabriel Nivasch

item.title: The bigraded Frobenius series of the wreath product superspace coinvariant rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.38875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the bigraded Frobenius series of the superspace coinvariant ring $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n}$ for the wreath products $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$, which is the quotient of the ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\otimes\bigwedge[\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n]$ of polynomial-valued differential forms by the ideal generated by diagonal $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$-invariants with vanishing constant term. The bigraded multiplicity of each irreducible character is a sum over standard Young $r$-tableaux of an expression determined by the flag major index and flag descent number. This refines the Frobenius series graded by fermionic degree found by Bhattacharya--Rhoades (2026). It specializes at $r=2$ to the hyperoctahedral group $\mathfrak{B}_n$ case, and it specializes at $r=1$ to recover the theorem of Murai--Rhoades--Wilson (2025) on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$. We give new formulas for the bigraded multiplicities of hook characters of the superspace coinvariant ring in types $A$ and $B$, yielding upper bounds on trigraded multiplicities of the sign character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$ and the determinant character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{B}_n}$. As a corollary, we deduce a conjecture of F. Bergeron (2024) on hook components of $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$.
item.dc:creator: Sutanay Bhattacharya, Sylvie Corteel, Yuhan Jiang, John Lentfer, Brendon Rhoades

item.title: Finite-size ignition laws near a vanishing branching deficit on near-regular simple graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.38912v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study heterogeneous bootstrap percolation on uniform simple graphs with prescribed degrees of mean $d\to\infty$ and deviations at most $C\sqrt d$. Thresholds are independently one with probability $(1-c/d)/d$ and two otherwise; seeds form an independent uniform set of prescribed size $a$. Let $T_a$ be the terminal number of active vertices and $b$ be one minus the mean number of threshold-one descendants of a reached vertex. Let $K\sim d^2$ be the quadratic response coefficient. If $b>0$ and $nb^3/K\to\infty$, we prove, uniformly over seed counts $a$, $ \mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)=\Phi(\frac{a-n\alpha_{\mathrm{det}}}{w})+o(1)$ with $w=\sqrt{nb/K}$, where $\alpha_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the exact empirical response-barrier center and $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. Put $a_0=(n/K)^{1/3}$. If $d^4/n\to0$, $a/a_0\to x>0$ and $\lambda=ba_0\to\ell\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)\to p(x,\ell)$, the one-sided Brownian parabolic survival probability. A sequential absolute-error law joins these regimes. A graphical counterexample shows that replacing the exact center by its leading term can cause limiting probability error $1/2$. The proof balances adaptive early-exploration transfer against late concentration at a tunable physical horizon, despite exponentially rare simplicity. We also prove quantitative and mesoscopic-seed refinements in explicitly narrower regimes. The only external graph-enumeration input is a stated reduction of McKay--Wormald's estimate; the probabilistic estimates for the cascade argument are proved in the text and appendices.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandr Rodionov

item.title: Anchored isoperimetry in percolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.38941v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that, for any infinite transitive graph $G$, the infinite cluster after supercritical percolation almost surely inherits the anchored isoperimetry of $G$. Moreover, the probability of violating the corresponding isoperimetric inequality decays exponentially in the isoperimetric profile of the host graph. This was previously known only for nonamenable transitive graphs, $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and very recently for transitive graphs of polynomial growth. Our proof combines the thinning-and-sprinkling technique with a novel counting algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Sahar Diskin, Lyuben Lichev, Ritvik Ramanan Radhakrishnan, Benny Sudakov, Laury Verhoeven

item.title: Borsuk number in four dimensions is at most seven
item.description: arXiv:2610.39078v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every bounded set of diameter one in four-dimensional Euclidean space can be covered by seven balls of diameter strictly smaller than $0.9999$. In particular, the Borsuk number satisfies $b_4\le7$. The proof combines geometric arguments based on contact points of the circumball with an exact finite computation. For small and large circumradius, the covering centres are constructed analytically. In the remaining range, a suitable triangle of contact points reduces the problem to a four-parameter family of ball polytopes. The parameter cube is subdivided into 23494 boxes. For each parameter box, candidate centres are found by nonlinear optimization, and the resulting covering is verified using exact rational interval arithmetic and paraboloid lifting.
item.dc:creator: Andrii Arman, Andriy Bondarenko, Andriy Prymak, Danylo Radchenko

item.title: CA2 numbers and the Riemann hypothesis: a numerical investigation of Ramanujan's inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.39120v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robin's criterion reduces the Riemann hypothesis to an inequality for colossally abundant (CA) numbers, and Wu's theorem reduces the test further to the subclass CA2. We study this reduction numerically and consider smaller subsets on which the same criterion remains sufficient. We also show that the logarithmic decay law suggested by Briggs's computations follows from Ramanujan's conditional bounds. To investigate the next term, we compare the normalized Robin difference with Ramanujan's oscillatory expression involving the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. The resulting difference has a slowly varying component on both CA and CA2. Its scaled values continue to vary over the computed range, leading to questions about convergence, upper bounds, and higher-order terms. We describe the sampling used in the figures and estimate the error from truncating the sum over zeros.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry R. Leshchiner, Oleg R. Musin, James Thompson

item.title: Generalized Discrete Fractal Dimensions of Graph Families
item.description: arXiv:2610.39187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantifying the self-similarity of complex networks via discrete fractal dimensions is a fundamental problem in network science. In this paper, we investigate some general fractal dimensions of graph families based on q-energy and R\'enyi entropy. We first establish several bounds for the energy, and then discuss the monotonicity, measure invariance of the dimensions, as well as some concrete graph families.
item.dc:creator: Jiantao Liu, Cheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Qingcheng Zeng

item.title: Local Convergence of Triadic Closures of Sparse Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39535v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Triadic closure is a natural mechanism for modeling the clustering phenomenon observed in many real-world networks. Given a possibly random undirected graph $H$, we consider pairs of non-adjacent vertices that have a common neighbor. Conditional on $H$, each such pair is joined by an edge independently and simultaneously, with a probability depending on the degrees of its endpoints and on the number of their common neighbors. The resulting graph is called a triadic closure of $H$. We study the effect of this operation on local convergence. More precisely, we prove that if a sequence of potentially random finite undirected graphs of $\left( H_n \right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges locally in probability to a rooted graph $H^*$, then the corresponding sequence of triadic closures converges locally in probability to the same triadic closure of $H^*$. As a consequence, we obtain a general limit theorem for the clustering coefficients of triadic closures. In particular, we show that the triadic closures can have a strictly positive limiting clustering coefficients even when the limiting clustering coefficients of the parent graph sequence is zero. Finally, we apply our results to several classical sparse random graph models including Erd\H{o}s-R\'{e}nyi, configuration, preferential attachment models and compute the limiting clustering coefficients of their triadic closures.
item.dc:creator: Himasish Talukdar

item.title: Topological Insights and Combinatorial Frameworks for Twist Knot Complements
item.description: arXiv:2610.39593v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The complement of a knot in $\mathbb{S}^3$ is a fundamental object in $3$-manifold topology and serves as a primary building block in the study of geometric structures on manifolds. For a large class of knots, these complements admit complete hyperbolic metrics, motivating the development of various frameworks for their classification and analysis. A twist knot is formed by applying a series of half-twists to a closed loop and linking the ends. In this article, we present explicit topological and combinatorial descriptions of all twist knot complements via the construction of suitable cell structures. Our method produces a closed $3$-dimensional pseudomanifold with a single vertex, arising from prescribed face pairings of a faceted $3$-ball. Removing the vertex yields the complement of the corresponding twist knot. The construction naturally induces ideal triangulations of these knot complements, several of which are shown to be facet-minimal. Beyond providing concrete models, our approach offers new perspectives on the topology of knot complements and leads to some open research problems.
item.dc:creator: Biplab Basak, Mangaldeep Saha, Ayushi Trivedi

item.title: Symbolic depth functions of edge ideals via local graph structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.39630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the depth of symbolic powers of edge ideals, focusing on local properties of graphs. First, we give several sufficient conditions for the symbolic depth function to be non-increasing, using local properties of graphs and local cohomology. Next, we give a counterexample to a conjecture of Minh, T.N. Trung, and Vu concerning the stable value of the symbolic depth function, where the difference between the conjectured value and the actual value can be arbitrary large. Finally, we study a conjecture of Muta stating the depth of a symbolic power of an edge ideal is at least that of the corresponding ordinary power. We prove it for graphs whose connected components are unicyclic or bipartite.
item.dc:creator: Yuji Muta, Naoki Terai

item.title: Four-Coloring Planar Graphs in Linear Time
item.description: arXiv:2610.39753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The famous Four Color Theorem (4CT) states that any planar graph can be colored with four colors, but how do we find a 4-coloring? In our previous paper [FOCS'26], we presented a simple combinatorial algorithm to 4-color planar graphs in $O(n\log n)$ time. We improve it here to $O(n)$ time, which is optimal. The algorithm from our previous paper is based on proving that every planar triangulation has a linear number of reducible configurations or obstructing cycles. The bottleneck for the algorithm is that we need $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes to extend a recursive 4-coloring to the reducible configurations. Each Kempe change can involve a constant fraction of the graph and takes linear time. Here we show that all $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes can be identified and implemented in $O(n)$ time. The idea is to spend $O(n)$ time to preprocess the graph so that we can identify and simulate each good Kempe change in $O(n/\log n)$ amortized time. Thus, we implement all $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes in $O(n)$ total time. Based on this, we implement the whole 4-coloring in linear time. We note that creating such a representation for fast identification and simulation of the right Kempe changes is a challenge of data structures, unlike the previous paper that builds on a new graph theoretic understanding of reducible configurations.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Inoue, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Atsuyuki Miyashita, Bojan Mohar, Carsten Thomassen, Mikkel Thorup

item.title: Exact Avoid-or-Compress Extrema for Dense Reachable Images: Defects Four and Five
item.description: arXiv:2610.39833v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $S$ be a reachable image of a strongly connected synchronizing automaton and $\varnothing\ne A\subsetneq S$. We determine the maximum shortest avoid-or-compress length over binary and arbitrary finite alphabets for $m=n-|S|=4$ and $m=5$. The exact values are $\min(n-|A|,11)$ and $\min(n-|A|,14)$, respectively. Uniform binary constructions attain both bounds. For the upper bounds, short-pair graphs and actual-image constraints reduce all parameters to finite necessary domains. Exhaustive checks exclude the domains, apart from a single relaxation eliminated by a multipartite overlap lemma. The largest calculation covers 3,206,988 domains.
item.dc:creator: Qichao Wang, Daoyu Dong

item.title: From Trees to Binary Trees: Approximation Algorithms and a PTAS
item.description: arXiv:2610.39863v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kellerhals, Krebs, Nichterlein, and Schmid introduced the optimization problem Tree in Binary Tree (TBT), where, given a tree $T$, the task is to find a binary tree $S^*$ with $V(T)=V(S^*)$ that minimizes $\sum_{uv\in E(T)} \operatorname{dist}_{S^*}(u,v)$. They also introduced the variant Tree in Binary Tree With Steiner Nodes (TBT-SN), where the condition $V(T)=V(S^*)$ is relaxed to $V(T)\subseteq V(S^*)$. We give a simple linear-time $\frac{8}{3}$-approximation algorithm for TBT and a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for TBT-SN. Our main building idea in both algorithms is to iteratively consider subtrees of the tree $T$ which contain all vertices below some vertex $v$ and construct a solution where $v$ has degree 1. For the PTAS, we cut $T$ into smaller trees, solve these instances, modify the obtained solutions, and combine them to achieve a solution for the original instance.
item.dc:creator: Fabian Weisbrodt, Florian Werner

item.title: Low-rank matrices with three prescribed off-diagonal values over $\mathbb{F}_p$
item.description: arXiv:2610.39908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime such that $2$ is a primitive root modulo $p$. We prove that, for every three-element set $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ and every integer $n\geq1$, there exists a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with zero diagonal, off-diagonal entries in $L$, and rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. This answers a question of Bukh for all such primes and, in particular, settles the case $L=\{1,4,6\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{19}$ singled out on his problem list. When $0\notin L$, a standard polynomial argument shows that the exponent $1/3$ is optimal. The proof combines a geometric construction in characteristic two with an incidence matrix factorization over $\mathbb{F}_p$. The same construction yields integer lifts $L'$ of the prescribed sets $L$ and symmetric $L'$-matrices of rational rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. When $0\notin L'$, this improves Bukh's general quadratic lower bound, giving matrices of order $\Omega_{p,L}(r^3)$ and rational rank at most $r$.
item.dc:creator: Firdavs Rakhmonov

item.title: Block-exchange descent for insertion: commuting projections and minimum masks
item.description: arXiv:2610.39941v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For fixed nonempty words $u,v$, the minimum insertion degree of a shuffle is the least number of inserted-source runs among its representations. We prove that, after a block exchange from a minimum mask of degree $r$, the minimum over masks with commuting source projections is exactly $r-1$; a larger decrease occurs precisely when a noncommuting mask has fewer runs. If either source is unary, every such exchange is exact. We prove an explicit repair for an infinite periodic degree-three family. Computer-assisted results establish first-mask descent through combined length seventeen over every alphabet, degree-three first-mask descent through length thirty, and a uniform repair of all degree-three failures through length thirty, including all further letter identifications. Counterexamples to arbitrary, first, and last minimum-mask choices explain the need for alternative masks. Finally, we prove that minimum iteration depths have no gaps for arbitrary languages. General block-exchange descent and Singleton No-Gap remain open.
item.dc:creator: Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang, Charles E. Hughes

item.title: Quasimodularity of $q$-series associated to root lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.40034v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by conjectures arising in part from the study of class-$\mathcal{S}$ vertex algebras associated with four-dimensional supersymmetric field theories, we study multiple $q$-zeta functions attached to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras. We prove their conjectured quasimodularity for all classical Lie algebras of types $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$, as well as a more general Weyl-symmetrized version in which the exponents attached to the positive roots are allowed to vary, under a suitable parity condition. Our proof is based on a substantially more general result. We introduce new combinatorial objects, called sets of level one and pairs of level two, which generalize the configurations arising from classical root systems. To these we associate multivariable lattice sums and prove that, under a natural admissibility condition, they are Fourier expansions of polar quasi-Jacobi forms of level one and level two, respectively. Quasimodularity of the Lie-theoretic $q$-series follows by specialization of the elliptic variables. The positive roots of type $A$ form a set of level one, and those of types $B$, $C$, and $D$ are described by pairs of level two. The proof combines a structural analysis of these new combinatorial configurations with reduction procedures and induction on the rank. The resulting framework applies to a much wider class of lattice sums than those coming from root systems and supports more general quasimodularity conjectures for $q$-series associated with integral hyperplane arrangements.
item.dc:creator: Antun Milas, Jan-Willem M. van Ittersum

item.title: Packing and covering random trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.40150v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the sizes of optimal packings and coverings of conditioned branching processes by balls with growing radii. We find a universal limiting constant, and thereby establish universality of packing and covering numbers across different scales and different offspring distributions. To be precise, for $\mu$ an offspring distribution with mean $1$ and finite variance $\sigma^2$ we let $T_n$ be a Bienaym\'e tree with offspring distribution $\mu$ conditioned to have size $n$. We prove that the packing number (resp. covering number) of $T_n$ with balls of radii $1\ll \gamma_n \ll n^{1/2}$ is asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C} n /(\sigma^2 \gamma_n^2)$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C} n /(4\sigma^2 \gamma_n^2)$), for a universal constant $\mathfrak{C}$. We also show that the order of limits can be exchanged and that the same limit occurs when we first consider the limiting covering number of $T_n$ by balls of fixed radius $R$, and thereafter let $R$ tend to $\infty$. We then extend these results to the Brownian continuum random tree conditioned to have mass $1$. For this model, we prove that the packing (resp. covering) number with balls of radii $\varepsilon$ are asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C}/\varepsilon^2$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C}/(4\varepsilon^2)$), for the same constant $\mathfrak{C}$, in contrast with a conjecture by Aldous. Finally, our results answer a question by Devroye, Eide and Pralat on the asymptotic burning number of mean $1$ finite variance Bienaym\'e trees of size $n$, by showing that it lies between $(c+o(1)) n^{1/3}$ and $(2c+o(1))n^{1/3}$ with high probability, for a constant $c$ that only depends on the offspring variance.
item.dc:creator: Caelan Atamanchuk, Simon Briend, Serte Donderwinkel, Elaine Herrera

item.title: Bounds on the Diagonal Degree of the Biadjoint Scalar Amplitude Matrix
item.description: arXiv:2610.40355v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Biadjoint scalar theory partial amplitudes, $m_n(\alpha,\beta)$, define an $(n-1)!/2\times (n-1)!/2$ matrix, $M_n$, with rows and columns labeled by orderings. The CHY construction of $M_n$ implies that its rank is $(n-3)!$. Invertible submatrices of maximal rank enter in the KLT construction relating graviton amplitudes to gluon amplitudes. Motivated by finding the KLT formula with the smallest number of terms, one of the authors posed the question of whether there is a critical $n_c$ such that for all $n>n_c$ there exists a diagonal submatrix of $M_n$ of rank $(n-3)!$. In this work we obtain bounds on the size of the largest non-singular diagonal submatrix of $M_n$, which we call its diagonal degree $\Delta_n$, and we answer the question in the negative. We prove that the diagonal degree is exponentially suppressed relative to the CHY rank: $\Delta_n/(n-3)! = \exp(-\Theta (n))$ as $n\to \infty$. More explicitly, we establish the bounds $\exp(-1.5n)\leq\Delta_n/(n-3)!\leq \exp \left[ -0.01n+O(1)\right]$.
item.dc:creator: Freddy Cachazo, Rajbir Longia

item.title: Half-Optimal Induced Matchings in Random Graphs: Online and Low-Degree Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2610.40369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For many optimization problems on random graphs, most prominently the largest independent set problem, natural algorithms reach only half the optimum, and such factor-two gaps are known to be sharp within broad algorithmic classes. We prove such a gap for finding large induced matchings in Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs. In the worst case, requiring a matching to be induced turns a polynomial-time solvable problem into an NP-hard one; our results reveal an average-case counterpart. In $G(n,p)$ with $C/n\le p\le 1-\kappa$, the largest induced matching has size $(1+o(1))L$ with high probability, where $L=\log_{1/(1-p)}(np)$. A simple online greedy algorithm finds an induced matching of size $(1/2-\epsilon)L$, while no online algorithm, even with adaptive inspection order and unbounded computation, finds one of size $(1/2+\epsilon)L$ except with probability $\exp(-\Omega(L\log(np)))$. In the sparse regime $p=d/n$, low-degree polynomial algorithms exhibit the same sharp threshold. Our guarantees rest on a maximality principle: with high probability, every maximal induced matching is half-optimal. Greedy outputs a maximal induced matching and our low-degree algorithm a near-maximal one. We bypass the delicate coupling arguments classically used to analyze greedy since Karp. For low-degree hardness, we adapt Wein's overlap gap argument, with forbidden structures that track overlaps between endpoint sets rather than edge sets, since a new edge may join two previously used endpoints and thus encounter no fresh randomness. For online hardness, we give a new and significantly simpler argument that avoids the correlated instances of prior OGP-based proofs: at a suitable stopping time, all pairs involving uninspected vertices remain unrevealed, so a direct first-moment bound suffices.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Dhawan, Eren C. K{\i}z{\i}lda\u{g}, Neeladri Maitra, Cheng Mao, Timothy L. H. Wee

item.title: Multiple representations in difference sets under polynomial density constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.40489v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the classical study of additive representation functions and the combinatorial phenomenon of sum-difference asymmetry, we investigate the subtractive representation function $d_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}}(n)$, which counts the number of solutions of the equation $n = b - a$ with $a\in \mathcal{A}$ and $b\in \mathcal{B}$. Specifically, we study lower bounds and the asymptotic behavior of $d_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}}(n)$ under polynomial density constraints of orders $x^\alpha$ and $x^{1-\alpha}$, where $0 < \alpha < 1$. We first establish a general lower bound for the first moment of $d_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}}(n)$. Furthermore, by employing a recursive construction, we prove that this lower bound is essentially optimal under certain regularity assumptions on the counting functions. Finally, utilizing probabilistic methods, we show the existence of sets for which $d_{\mathcal{B},\mathcal{A}}(n)$ has a logarithmic point-wise upper bound.
item.dc:creator: Yuchen Ding, S\'andor Z. Kiss, Wei Niu, P\'eter P\'al Pach, Csaba S\'andor

item.title: Directed Cut-Query Complexity of Finding a King
item.description: arXiv:2610.40521v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A king in a tournament is a vertex from which every other vertex is reachable by a directed path of length at most two. We study the deterministic query complexity of finding a king when a query specifies a set of vertices and returns the number of edges directed from that set to its complement. We prove that this complexity is $\Theta(n)$ for $n$-vertex tournaments. To show this, we first show that every correct deterministic algorithm in this model must output a maximum-outdegree vertex, even though a king need not have maximum outdegree. We then give an adversary whose answers, after too few queries, remain consistent with a tournament in which the algorithm's output does not have maximum outdegree.
item.dc:creator: Ziad Ismaili Alaoui, Oded Lachish, Nikhil S. Mande

item.title: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II
item.description: arXiv:2610.40571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We confirm a conjecture of the first author [SODA'26] on a strong form of pseudo-telepathy for Khot's $d$-to-$1$ games: for every $d\geq 4$, every $\epsilon>0$, and every $k\in\mathbb N$, there is a $d$-to-$1$ label-cover game of classical value less than $\epsilon$ that admits a perfect quantum strategy using finite-dimensional shared entanglement with measurement contexts of radius at least $k$. As a consequence, there exist graphs whose quantum chromatic number $\chi_q$ is $3$ and whose classical chromatic number $\chi$ is arbitrarily large. This is the first improvement on the quantum chromatic gap since the work of Brassard, Cleve, and Tapp [Phys. Rev. Lett.'99], which produced graphs for which $\chi$ grows exponentially in $\chi_q$. To prove the conjecture, we proceed as follows. We start with a ``stretched'' version of the Mermin--Peres magic square, obtained by spacing out its equations and linking them with additional long equation wires. This operation increases the radius of the initial measurement contexts of a perfect quantum strategy for the game, while preserving classical unsatisfiability. We then apply parallel repetition to make the classical value small, and we turn the system into a pseudo-telepathic multi-layered Kneser hypergraph via a PCP construction of Dinur, Guruswami, Khot, and Regev [STOC'03]. Finally, we feed the resulting hypergraph into the reduction of Fei, Minzer, and Wang from hypergraph colouring to $4$-to-$1$ games, we establish quantum completeness of this reduction, and we show that it preserves context radius.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Ciardo, Antoine Mottet

item.title: An Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.40590v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a graph $G$, does it have quantum symmetries, or in other words, is the algebra of the quantum automorphism group non-commutative? In the world of ordinary groups, determining whether a finitely presented group is commutative is undecidable. This is an immediate consequence of the Adian-Rabin theorem, which shows that many natural properties of finitely presented groups are undecidable. In this paper, we prove an Adian-Rabin theorem for quantum automorphism groups of graphs, showing that many natural properties of the quantum automorphism group of a graph (including having quantum symmetries) are undecidable. We also show that it's undecidable to determine if the discrete quantum automorphism group is non-trivial. Our methods are based on solution groups of linear system nonlocal games, and we also prove an Adian-Rabin theorem in this context.
item.dc:creator: Josse van Dobben de Bruyn, William Slofstra

item.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 10: Type-2 isomorphic $C_{np^3}(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = $p$ and related groups
item.description: arXiv:2211.06970v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article is the $10^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}. In this part, we obtain families of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs $C_{np^3}(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = $p$, and related Abelian groups where $p$ is a prime number and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Theorems \ref{c1} and \ref{c4} are the main results. In Theorem \ref{c4}, it is proved that for $i$ = 1 to $p$, circulant graphs $C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i)$ are isomorphic of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = $p$ and they form Abelian group $(T2_{np^3,p}(C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i)), \circ)$ where $T2_{np^3,p}(C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i))$ = $\{\theta_{np^3,p,jn}(C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i))$ = $C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_{i+j}) :$ $j$ = $0,1,...,p-1$ and $i+j$ in $C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_{i+j})$ is calculated under addition modulo $p \}$, $1 \leq x \leq p-1$, $0 \leq y \leq np - 1$, $1 \leq x+yp \leq np^2-1$, $y\in\mathbb{N}_0$, $p,np^3-p\in R^{np^3,x+yp}_i$ and $i,n,x\in\mathbb{N}$. Using Theorem \ref{c4}, a list of $T2_{np^3,p}(C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i))$, each containing $p$ isomorphic circulant graphs $C_{np^3}(R^{np^3,x+yp}_i)$ of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = $p$, for $p$ = 3,5,7, $n$ = 1,2 and $y$ = 0 is given in the Annexure and more such families of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs are presented in \cite{v24}.
item.dc:creator: Vilfred Kamalappan, Wilson Peraprakash

item.title: Schubert puzzles and integrability III: separated descents
item.description: arXiv:2306.13855v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In paper I of this series we gave positive formulae for expanding the product $\mathfrak S^\pi \mathfrak S^\rho$ of two Schubert polynomials, in the case that both $\pi,\rho$ had shared descent set of size $\leq 3$. Here we introduce and give positive formulae for two new classes of Schubert product problems: separated descent in which $\pi$'s last descent occurs at (or before) $\rho$'s first, and almost separated descent in which $\pi$'s last two descents occur at (or before) $\rho$'s first two respectively. In both cases our puzzle formulae extend to $K$-theory (multiplying Grothendieck polynomials), and in the separated descent case, to equivariant $K$-theory. The two formulae arise (via quantum integrability) from fusion of minuscule quantized loop algebra representations in types $A$, $D$ respectively.
item.dc:creator: Allen Knutson, Paul Zinn-Justin

item.title: Chordal matroids arising from generalized parallel connections II
item.description: arXiv:2405.02099v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1961, Dirac showed that chordal graphs are exactly the graphs that can be constructed from complete graphs by a sequence of clique-sums. In an earlier paper, by analogy with Dirac's result, we introduced the class of $GF(q)$-chordal matroids as those matroids that can be constructed from projective geometries over $GF(q)$ by a sequence of generalized parallel connections across projective geometries over $GF(q)$. Our main result showed that when $q=2$, such matroids have no induced minor in $\{M(C_4),M(K_4)\}$. In this paper, we show that the class of $GF(2)$-chordal matroids coincides with the class of binary matroids that have none of $M(K_4)$, $M^*(K_{3,3})$, or $M(C_n)$ for $n\geq 4$ as a flat. We also show that $GF(q)$-chordal matroids can be characterized by an analogous result to Rose's 1970 characterization of chordal graphs as those that have a perfect elimination ordering of vertices.
item.dc:creator: James Dylan Douthitt, James Oxley

item.title: The $q$-deformed random-to-random family in the Hecke algebra
item.description: arXiv:2503.17580v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We generalize Reiner--Saliola--Welker's well-known but mysterious family of *$k$-random-to-random shuffles* from Markov chains on symmetric groups to Markov chains on Type-$A$ Iwahori--Hecke algebras. We prove that these operators pairwise commute, and that their eigenvalues are polynomials in $q$ with non-negative integer coefficients; we express these eigenvalues in a closed form as certain symmetric function evaluations (which is new even for $q=1$). We show that these operators are simultaneously diagonalizable for almost all $q$, and combinatorially express the dimension of the subalgebra they generate. Our work generalizes and extends work of Reiner--Saliola--Welker and Lafreni\`ere for the symmetric group, and simplifies all known proofs in this case.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Brauner, Patricia Commins, Darij Grinberg, Franco Saliola

item.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 2: Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs of orders 16, 24, 27
item.description: arXiv:2508.09384v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article is the $2^{nd}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}. Definition of Type-2 isomorphism of circulant graphs $C_n(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ modified in \cite{v2-2-arX} was further modified to definition \ref{d6} in \cite{v2-1} by the author by considering $m > 1$ divides $\gcd(n, r)$, $m^3$ divides $n$ and $r\in R$ and studied Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs w.r.t. $m$ = 2. In this paper, using the modified definition \ref{d6}, we obtain all 8 and 32 number of pairs of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs of orders 16 and 24, respectively and all 27 number of triples of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs of order 27.
item.dc:creator: Vilfred Kamalappan

item.title: An upper bound for the list-distinguishing chromatic number of $K_{r,r+1}$-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2509.11992v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2006, Collins and Trenk obtained a general sharp upper bound for the distinguishing chromatic number of a connected graph. Inspired by Catlin's combinatorial techniques from 1978, we establish improved upper bounds for classes of connected graphs that have only small complete bigraphs as induced subgraphs. In this framework, we also consider the list-distinguishing chromatic number of such graphs. We apply Menger's theorem to demonstrate applications of our main result for graphs whose constructions are based on Paley graphs and Cayley graphs on Dihedral groups.
item.dc:creator: Amitayu Banerjee

item.title: Magic Gems: Convex Hulls of Lifted Magic Squares
item.description: arXiv:2512.09170v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given an arrangement of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ in an $n\times n$ grid, we lift each cell to $\mathbb{R}^3$ by centring its grid coordinates $(x,y)$ at the origin and taking its centred entry $z = s_{ij} - (n^2+1)/2$ as a vertical height. The convex hull of these $n^2$ points is the gem of the arrangement, whose lower and upper boundaries are the regular subdivisions of the grid induced by $\pm z$. While random arrangements and generic linear magic squares have gems whose vertex counts grow with $n$, our main theorem shows that the classical Siamese (de la Loub\`ere) magic square of every odd order $n\ge5$ has $f$-vector $(12,26,16)$, isometry group $\{\pm\mathrm{id}\}$, and only the twelve vertices forced by the boundary of the grid. The proof shears the lift onto five horizontal terraces and reduces the hull calculation to a finite table of polynomials in $m=(n-1)/2$; the same method gives $f$-vector $(12,24,14)$ for the base-$n$ digit-exchanged square. Along any family of linear squares with fixed steps the $f$-vector is eventually periodic in $n$, whereas over all linear magic squares of prime order $n$ the maximum vertex count grows as $\Theta(\ln n)$. Whenever the heights have vanishing first moments, a short principal-axes argument shows that the point set has a non-trivial isometry if and only if the arrangement is self-complementary up to dihedral symmetry. An exact census of the $880$ magic squares of order four yields $616$ congruence classes and $352$ combinatorial types of gems, and shows that while vertex and facet counts are nearly insensitive to the magic line-sum conditions, the volume and solid centroid shift systematically.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Elliott Mathewson

item.title: How to Tropicalize a non-Archimedean Lattice
item.description: arXiv:2512.12127v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a method for computing the tropicalization of a lattice over the valuation ring of a non-Archimedean field. Our construction relies on the entropy polynomial, a tropical polynomial whose coefficients are determined by the valuations of minors of a matrix representing the lattice. We show that the tropicalization of the lattice is the support of a polyhedral complex defined through this polynomial. Moreover, we prove that this tropicalization is a finitely generated tropical semimodule over the nonnegative tropical scalars and provide explicit generators in terms of the entropy vector of the lattice. Finally, we extend our construction to valuated bimatroids, establishing analogous results beyond the realizable setting.
item.dc:creator: Yassine Elmaazouz

item.title: Arboreal Networks and Ultrametrics
item.description: arXiv:2601.04836v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ultrametrics are an important class of distances used in applications such as phylogenetics, clustering and classification theory. Ultrametrics are essentially distances that can be represented by an edge-weighted rooted tree so that all of the distances in the tree from the root to any leaf of the tree are equal. In this paper, we introduce a generalization of ultrametrics called arboreal ultrametrics which have applications in phylogenetics and also arise in the theory of distance-hereditary graphs. These are partial distances, that is distances that are not necessarily defined for every pair of elements in the groundset, that can be represented by an ultrametric arboreal network, that is, an edge-weighted rooted network whose underlying graph is a tree. As with ultrametrics all of the distances in the ultrametric arboreal network from any root to any leaf below it are are equal but, in contrast, the network may have more than one root. In our two main results we characterize when a partial distance is an arboreal ultrametric as well as proving that, somewhat surprisingly, given any unrooted edge-weighted phylogenetic tree there is a necessarily unique way to insert roots into this tree so as to obtain an arboreal ultrametric.
item.dc:creator: Katharina T. Huber, Vincent Moulton, Guillaume E. Scholz

item.title: Simplicial spheres with $g_k=1$
item.description: arXiv:2601.10072v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $d\geq 4$, Kalai (1987) characterized all simplicial $(d-1)$-spheres with $g_2=0$, and for $k\geq 2$ and $d\geq 2k$, Murai and Nevo (2013) characterized all simplicial $(d-1)$-spheres with $g_k=0$. In addition, for $d\geq 4$, Nevo and Novinsky (2011) characterized all simplicial $(d-1)$-spheres with $g_2=1$. Motivated by these results, we characterize, for any $k\geq 2$ and $d\geq 2k+1$, all simplicial $(d-1)$-spheres with no missing faces of dimension larger than $d-k$ that satisfy $g_k=1$. When $d=2k$, we obtain a characterization of simplicial $(d-1)$-spheres with $g_k=1$ and no missing faces of dimension greater than $k$, under the additional assumption that there exists at least one missing face of dimension $k$. Finally, for $k=3$, we are able to remove this assumption and characterize all simplicial $5$-spheres with no missing faces of dimension larger than $3$ that satisfy $g_3=1$.
item.dc:creator: Isabella Novik, Hailun Zheng

item.title: The Poincar\'e polynomial of the type B analogue of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n+1}$
item.description: arXiv:2603.01956v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish formulas for the Poincar\'e polynomial of the type B analogue of the Deligne--Knudsen--Mumford moduli space of rational curves with n marked points, providing type B counterparts to results by Keel, Manin, Getzler, and Yuzvinsky. We establish functional and differential equations satisfied by the bivariate exponential generating function of these polynomials. We show how this generating function relates to the classical one in type A. We deduce the gamma-positivity of these polynomials via a quadratic recursion and discuss a type B analogue of a formula found by Aluffi, Marcolli and Nascimento in type A.
item.dc:creator: Luis Ferroni, Roberto Pagaria, Lorenzo Vecchi

item.title: Towards the characterization of minimum weight codewords of Schubert codes
item.description: arXiv:2603.14247v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A formula for the minimum weight of Schubert codes was conjectured by Ghorpade and Lachaud in 2000. This was established by Xiang in 2008. In 2018, Ghorpade and Singh provided a new proof of this conjecture. Moreover, they also conjectured that the minimum weight codewords of the Schubert codes $C_\a (\ell, m)$ are given by the so-called \emph{Schubert decomposable codewords}. We prove the validity of the conjecture for all Schubert varieties $\Omega_{\a}(\ell, V_m)$ for all but finitely many values of $q$.
item.dc:creator: Mrinmoy Datta, Tiasa Dutta, Trygve Johnsen

item.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 1: Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs $C_n(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = 2
item.description: arXiv:2605.11441v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article is the first part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}. Circulant graphs $C_n(R)$ and $C_n(S)$ are said to be \emph{Adam's isomorphic} if there exist some $a\in \mathbb{Z}_n^*$ such that $S = a R$ under arithmetic reflexive modulo $n$ \cite{ad67}. In 1970, Elspas and Turner \cite{eltu} raised a question on the isomorphism of $C_{16}(1,3,7)$ and $C_{16}(2,3,5)$. The author \cite{v96} further modify the definition to $m$ and $m^3$ are divisors of $\gcd(n, r)$ and $n$, respectively, and $r\in R$. Using the modified definition \ref{d16}, we present our study on Type-2 isomorphism of circulant graphs $C_n(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = 2. We reprove that $(i)$ $C_{16}(1,2,7)$ and $C_{16}(2,3,5)$ are Type-2 isomorphic w.r.t. $m$ = 2; $(ii)$ For $n \geq 2$, $k \geq 3$, $1 \leq 2s-1 \leq 2n-1$, $n \neq 2s-1$, $R$ = $\{2, 2s-1, 4n-(2s-1)\}$ and $S$ = $\{2, 2n-(2s-1), 2n+2s-1\}$, $C_{8n}(R)$ and $C_{8n}(S)$ are Type-2 isomorphic w.r.t. $m$ = 2, $n,s\in\mathbb{N}$; and $(iii)$ For $n \geq 2$, $1 \leq 2s-1 < 2s'-1 \leq [\frac{n}{2}]$, $0 \leq t \leq [\frac{n}{2}]$, $R$ = $\{2,2s-1, 2s'-1\}$ and $n,s,s'\in \mathbb{N}$, if $\theta_{n,2,t}(C_n(R))$ and $C_n(R)$ are isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 2 for some $t$, then $n \equiv 0~(mod ~ 8)$, $2s-1+2s'-1$ = $\frac{n}{2}$, $2s-1 \neq \frac{n}{8}$, $t$ = $\frac{n}{8}$ or $\frac{3n}{8}$, $1 \leq 2s-1 \leq \frac{n}{4}$ and $n \geq 16$ where $\theta_{n,m,t}$ is a transformation used to define Type-2 isomorphism of a circulant graph. At the end, we present a VB program POLY215.EXE which shows how Type-2 isomorphism w.r.t. $m$ = 2 of $C_{8n}(R)$ takes place for $R = \{2, 2s-1, 4n-(2s-1)\}$, $n \geq 2$ and $n,s\in {\mathbb N}$.

item.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 5: Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs of orders 48, 81, 96
