item.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 6: Abelian groups $(T2_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$ and $(V_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$
item.description: arXiv:2605.12868v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article is the $6^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}. In this part, we define $V_{n,m}(C_n(R))$ and Type-2 set $T2_{n,m}(C_n(R))$ of $C_n(R)$ and present their properties. We prove that $(V_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$ is an Abelian group and $(T2_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$ is a subgroup of $(V_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$ where $T2_{n,m}(C_n(R))$ = $\{C_n(R)\}$ $\cup$ $\{C_n(S):$ $C_n(S)$ is Typ-2 isomorphic to $C_n(R)$ w.r.t. $m \}$ and $(T2_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$ is the Type-2 group of $C_n(R)$ w.r.t. $m$. We also present many examples of Type-1 and Type-2 groups where $T1_{n}(C_n(R))$ = $\{C_n(xR): x\in\varphi_{n}\}$ is the Type-1 set of $C_n(R)$ and $(T1_{n}(C_n(R)), \circ')$ is its Type-1 group.
item.dc:creator: Vilfred Kamalappan

item.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. PART 9: Computer programs to show Type-1 $\&$ -2 isomorphic circulant graphs
item.description: arXiv:2605.14140v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Elspas and Turner \cite{eltu} raised a question on the isomorphism of $C_{16}(1,3,7)$ and $C_{16}(2,3,5)$ and Vilfred \cite{v96} gave its answer by defining Type-2 isomorphism of $C_n(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ $\ni$ $m$ = $\gcd(n, r) > 1$ and also modified to $m$ and $m^3$ divides $\gcd(n, r)$ and $n$, respectively, $r\in R$ and $r,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and studied such graphs \cite{v13,v20, v2-1}. Using a $C^{++}$ computer program, the authors obtained families of Type-2 isomorphic $C_{n}(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = 2,3,5,7 for $n\in\mathbb{N}$ as well as $C_{np^3}(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = $p$ where $p$ is a prime and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. In this paper, we present the $C^{++}$ program and also a VB program POLY415.EXE which is used to show how Type-1 and Type-2 isomorphisms of a circulant graph take place as well as for checking and finding Type-1 and Type-2 circulant graphs of a given order. This article is the $9^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}.
item.dc:creator: Vilfred Kamalappan, Wilson Peraprakash

item.title: A Study on Type-2 Isomorphic Circulant Graphs: Part 7: $C_{432}(R)$, $C_{6750}(S)$ - each has 2 types of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs
item.description: arXiv:2605.14402v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this study, we obtain two families of circulant graphs, (i) family of circulant graphs $C_{432}(R)$, each has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 2 as well as $m$ = 3; and (ii) family of circulant graphs $C_{6750}(S)$, each has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 3 as well as $m$ = 5. This article is the $7^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}.
item.dc:creator: Vilfred Kamalappan

item.title: Domination in Johnson graphs J(n, 3) for odd n
item.description: arXiv:2606.10326v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2025 Cornet, Dravec, and Torres determined the domination number $\gamma(J(n,3))$ of the Johnson graph for every even $n \ge 6$, expressing it as a closed form $\phi_n$ in terms of Fort-Hedlund covering numbers, and conjectured the same value for odd $n$. We prove this conjecture: $\gamma(J(n,3)) = \phi_n$ for every odd $n \ge 7$. A dominating set of $J(n,3)$ is the same as a lotto design $\mathrm{LD}(n,3,3,2)$, and the lotto numbers $L(n,3,3,2)$, and hence $\gamma(J(n,3))$, were already determined for every $n$ by Bate (1978) and by Brouwer (1981). The contribution of this paper is therefore a new proof of the odd case, carried out within the bijective framework of Cornet, Dravec, and Torres.
item.dc:creator: Seung-ah Lee, Semin Oh

item.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 8: Isomorphism series, digraph and graph of $C_n(R)$
item.description: arXiv:2606.20984v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article is the $8^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}. In this study, we define {\em isomorphic set}, {\em isomorphism series}, {\em isomorphism digraph} or {\em isomorphism diagram} $\mathcal{D}$ and {\em isomorphism graph} $\mathcal{G}$ of circulant graphs and obtain these corresponding to $C_{16}(R)$, $C_{27}(S)$ and $C_{54}(1,3,17,19)$ and present the isomorphism digraph and the isomorphism graph of $C_{432}(T)$ which has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 2,3 and of $C_{6750}(U)$ which has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 3,5 where $T$ = $\{16, 27, 48, 54, 128, 160, 189\}$ and $U$ = $\{135, 243, 250, 750, 1107, 1593, 2000, 2457, 2500, 2943\}$. We also define {\em diameter of isomorphic set} of $C_n(R)$ and {\em isomorphic distance} between any two circulant graphs. We find that the order of isomorphic sets of $C_{432}(T)$ and $C_{6750}(U)$ are 36 and 450 and their diameters are 3 and 3, respectively.
item.dc:creator: V. Vilfred Kamalappan

item.title: Coloring t-perfect graphs with fewer colors
item.description: arXiv:2607.05961v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, Chudnovsky, Cook, Davies, Oum, and Tan obtained the first finite bound on the chromatic number of t-perfect graphs, showing that they are 199053-colorable. We improve this bound to 130 by refining their proof. The original proof establishes that every graph with large odd girth and large chromatic number contains a certain structure called an r-arithmetic rope, and that its existence in a certain leveling of a graph with large odd girth would imply an odd wheel as a t-minor, a known obstruction to t-perfectness. While their technique requires a lower bound on the chromatic number that is exponential in r, we show that the existence of an r-arithmetic rope can already be guaranteed under a linear bound. Using a slightly weakened notion of arithmetic ropes allows us to reduce the bound even further.
item.dc:creator: Matija Novakovi\'c, Stefan Weltge

item.title: Multiplier obstructions for Legendre pairs of length 333
item.description: arXiv:2607.20765v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A Legendre pair of length 333 would yield a Hadamard matrix of order 668, the smallest order presently unresolved by the Hadamard conjecture. We study the structured case in which both sequences are fixed by a common subgroup $H\leq(\mathbb Z/333\mathbb Z)^\times$ acting by coordinate multiplication. We prove that such a pair can exist only when $|H|\leq 6$. After a mod-3 compression reduces the problem to an order-108 kernel, there are exactly 30 subgroups. We exclude 21 of them, including all 19 subgroups of order at least 9. The final order-9 subgroup is eliminated analytically: its orbit structure restricts the 9-compressed entries to $\{\pm1,\pm17,\pm19,\pm35,\pm37\}$; the Legendre equations force a $+17,-17$ pair in one compressed sequence, and a single-shift autocorrelation bound then contradicts the required compressed correlation. The remaining exclusions use full-image compression, a row-sum congruence, exact meet-in-the-middle enumeration, and proof-carrying pseudo-Boolean encodings. The solver-assisted cases are accompanied by independently checked DRAT proofs or direct arithmetic certificates. The result constrains fixed common-multiplier symmetry only; the unrestricted existence problems remain open.
item.dc:creator: Arthur F. Ramos, David B. Hulak, Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

item.title: A Hopf algebra on permutations with a coupling product
item.description: arXiv:2607.23345v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define a coupling product and a draw coproduct on permutations and show that they define a graded, connected, cocommutative, free Hopf algebra $\mathbb{KS}$. In characteristic zero, this implies that $\mathbb{KS}$ is isomorphic to a certain cocommutative Hopf algebra associated with the dual of the coradical filtration of the Malvenuto--Reutenauer Hopf algebra on permutations. The coupling product and draw coproduct are permutation analogues of the product and coproduct on the monomial basis of symmetric functions; therefore, we can say that our presentation is a monomial basis for $\mathbb{KS}$.
item.dc:creator: Huilan Li, Yishuo Yang, Nantel Bergeron

item.title: Explicit and logarithmically improved chromatic bounds for $(P_2\cup P_3)$-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2607.23441v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every $(P_2\cup P_3)$-free graph $G$, with $k=\omega(G)$, satisfies \[ \chi(G)=O\!\left(k^3\frac{\ln\ln k}{\ln k}\right). \] Thus the class admits an $o(k^3)$ binding function. We also prove the explicit bound \[ \chi(G)\le \frac{k^3}{8}+\frac{5k^2}{4}-4k+8 \qquad(k\ge8), \] with a sharper formula for odd $k$. A further refinement gives an explicit cubic bound with leading coefficient $104/837<1/8$.
item.dc:creator: Lizhong Chen

item.title: On colorful Helly numbers and the growth of Tverberg numbers
item.description: arXiv:2608.06437v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish new bounds on colorful Helly and Tverberg numbers in abstract convexity spaces with Radon number $r$. We show that the colorful Helly number is at most $(r-1)2^r$, improving Holmsen--Lee's bound $r^{r^{O(\log r)}}$ and matching the known lower bound $2^{r-1}-1$ up to a factor $O(r)$. Furthermore, we prove that the Tverberg number is $r_k=O(r^{\lceil \log_2 r\rceil }k)$, reducing P\'alv\"olgyi's coefficient $r^{r^{r^{O(\log r)}}}$ to a quasipolynomial function of $r$. For $S_4$-separable spaces, we prove $r_k=O(r^2k)$. In the other direction, we construct a sequence of $S_4$-separable spaces with Tverberg number $r_k=\Omega(r^2k)$. This shows that the weak Eckhoff conjecture, asserting that $r_k=O(rk)$ in any abstract convexity space, fails already in separable spaces. The same construction refutes the analogue of Reay's conjecture in separable spaces.
item.dc:creator: Chaya Keller, Skand Parvatikar, Tuan Tran

item.title: Caged subsequences in permutations
item.description: arXiv:2608.09770v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a sequence $\mathfrak{a}:=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ of reals, a subsequence $\mathfrak{b}=(a_{i_1},\ldots,a_{i_k})$ is said to be "caged" if the largest and smallest among the members of $\mathfrak{b}$ are $a_{i_1}$ and $a_{i_k}$, though not necessarily in that order. In this paper, we consider the problem of maximal caged sequences in permutations $\pi\in S_n$. We also consider the same problem for a random permutation, both when the permutation is chosen uniformly at random and also when it is picked uniformly at random from among the permutations of rectangular shape, via the RSK correspondence. We also give a $O(n\log n)$ time algorithm to obtain these maximal caged sequences. In addition, we propose a randomized linear time algorithm that gives the length of the maximal caged sequence up to the factor of $(1-o(1))$.
item.dc:creator: Niranjan Balachandran, Omkar Ramdas, Umesh Shankar

item.title: Equilateral Completion in Floretion Triangular Coordinates: Locality, Product Points, and Reflection Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2608.15925v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study nondegenerate equilateral triangles whose vertices are centroids of the $4^n$ order-$n$ floretion tiles. Scaled integer triangular coordinates give exact equilateral completions and, by an obstruction modulo $3$, show that all three vertices have the same tile orientation. In particular, the complete triangle family and its synchronized local cyclic subfamily have respective sizes $|E_n|=\frac{4^n(4^n-1)}{12},\quad |L_n|=\frac{7^n-4^n}{3},$ so the local proportion tends to zero. Our principal new result answers the radial-homogeneity question left open in the preceding revision: for every order, the number of triangles containing a given tile is given by an exact affine formula in its squared scaled centroid radius. Although the two tile orientations have different formulas, their attainable squared radii belong to disjoint residue classes modulo $3$, yielding a single radial-incidence law on the full centroid set. We also determine local and nonlocal vertex incidences and obtain circular-shell and squared-radius moment identities. The unsigned vertex product defines an algebraic product point. By a rigidity theorem of Ma and Zhang, the multiplication-generated triangles are precisely the nontrivial global cyclic orbits; combining this with our geometric shell classification, we show that the product point is the origin exactly when the Euclidean triangle center is the origin. Further results enumerate central-vertex, no-$e$, and main-axis families, derive Fibonacci and finite-state recurrences for product-centered and reflection-restricted classes, and characterize pairwise anticommutation.
item.dc:creator: Creighton Dement

item.title: On the real-rootedness of Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of $(132,213)$-avoiding permutahedra
item.description: arXiv:2609.06096v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $P_d$ be the convex hull of the permutations of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ that avoid the patterns $132$ and $213$, and let $H_d(t)$ be its Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomial. We prove that all zeros of $H_d(t)$ are real and negative for $3\le d\le1000$ and for every $d\ge2^{62}$; for $d\le2$ the polynomial is constant. Expanding $H_d(t)$ in refined Eulerian polynomials does not suffice, since a coordinate is already negative at $d=7$. Let $A_{d,i}(t)$ enumerate all permutations of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with first entry $i$ by number of descents. For $c\ge0$, we prove that every nonnegative linear combination of $A_{d,1},\ldots,A_{d,d}$ and the adjacent differences $A_{d,r+1}-cA_{d,r}$, $2\le r\le d-2$, is real-rooted for all $d\ge4$ simultaneously if and only if $c\le2-\sqrt3$. This reduces real-rootedness to the positivity of explicit weighted tails of the coordinates. An exact certificate checks these inequalities for $d\le1000$, and coefficient estimates based on Darroch's theorem on the mode of a sum of Bernoulli variables prove them for $d\ge2^{62}$; the range $1001\le d<2^{62}$ remains open. Along the way we identify $P_d$, up to lattice equivalence, with twice a chain-poset permutahedron and with the Newton polytope of a discriminant, which transfers the known cube structure and volume of these models to $P_d$. We also show that the coefficient of $t^{d-1}$ in $H_d(t)$ counts strong tournament score sequences for $d\ge3$, confirming a conjecture of Rehberg in this range.
item.dc:creator: Pedro M. M. de Castro

item.title: Existence of regular sets in circulant quartic graphs: a complete characterization
item.description: arXiv:2609.09414v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Gamma=(V,E)$ be a graph and let $a,b$ be nonnegative integers. A nonempty proper subset $C\subset V$ is an \emph{$(a,b)$-regular set} if each vertex of $C$ has exactly $a$ neighbors in $C$ and each vertex outside $C$ has exactly $b$ neighbors in $C$. Perfect codes and total perfect codes are the $(0,1)$- and $(1,1)$-regular sets. For every connected circulant quartic graph $\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_n,\{x^{\pm k},x^{\pm\ell}\})$ and every pair $(a,b)$ we decide, in terms of $n$, $k$ and $\ell$, whether an $(a,b)$-regular set exists. Existence is proved by exhibiting unions of residue classes; non-existence comes from a Fourier-analytic obstruction combined with the fact that certain sums of roots of unity cannot vanish.
item.dc:creator: A. Abdollahi, J. Bagherian, F. Jafari, M. Khatami, Z. Shokoohi, R. Sobhani

item.title: Unimodality shenanigans in Ehrhart theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.10513v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct counterexamples to a four-decade-old conjecture attributed to Stanley concerning the unimodality of $h^*$-polynomials of IDP polytopes. As additional applications of our main constructions, we also disprove a conjecture by Brenti on the log-concavity of $h^*$-polynomials of Gorenstein IDP polytopes, and a conjecture by Ferroni and Higashitani concerning the log-concavity of the Ehrhart series of IDP polytopes. We also answer their question about the existence of very ample polytopes with non-log-concave interior Ehrhart series. Our class of examples arises by taking Cayley sums of rectangular prisms, and hence they possess regular unimodular flag triangulations by a result of Haase, Paffenholz, Piechnik and Santos. Remarkably, for the unimodality conjecture we can even find smooth counterexamples.
item.dc:creator: Luis Ferroni

item.title: First-Derivative Chromatic Symmetric Reconstruction For Proper Trees
item.description: arXiv:2609.13464v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Richard Stanley asked whether every tree $T$ is determined up to isomorphism by its chromatic symmetric function $X_T$. We approach this open problem by regarding $X_T$ as a polynomial in the power-sum symmetric functions $p_1, p_2, \dots$ and studying the invariant $\Phi_T = \left.\frac{\partial {X_T}}{\partial p_1}\right\rvert_{p_1 = 0}$. We prove that $\Phi_T$ distinguishes, among proper trees, every proper tree in which any non-leaf vertex with two or more non-leaf neighbors has a number of leaf neighbors occurring at no other non-leaf vertex. We give an equivalent formulation of Stanley's question in terms of $\Phi_T$. Finally, we show that counts of spanning forests with at most $t$ edges cannot distinguish all $k$-vertex trees when $t<\left\lfloor k/2\right\rfloor$, for every $k\ge4$.
item.dc:creator: Saad A. Awan

item.title: A Note on a Result of Chen Li: the Thinning Problem via the Kernel Method
item.description: arXiv:2609.18458v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, C. Li posted a preprint that resolves the fractional version of Talagrand's discrete convexity problem. In this note, we use the method of C. Li to answer another problem of Talagrand.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Fang, Tianyu Wang

item.title: Two-disjoint-cycle-cover edge bipancyclicity in Cartesian products
item.description: arXiv:2609.23031v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For two even integers $r_1\leq r_2$, a graph $G$ of even order is \emph{2-DCC edge $[r_1,r_2]$-bipancyclic} if for every ordered pair $(e,f)$ of independent edges and every even integer $\ell\in[r_1,r_2]$, there exist two vertex-disjoint cycles $C_1$ and $C_2$ with $V(C_1)\cup V(C_2)=V(G)$, $|C_1|=\ell$, $|C_2|=|V(G)|-\ell$, $e\in E(C_1)$, and $f\in E(C_2)$. We study this property for Cartesian products $G=H_1\square\cdots\square H_d$ with $d\geq2$, where each factor is $K_2$ or an even-order bipartite edge-Hamiltonian graph. We prove that $G$ is 2-DCC edge $[4,|V(G)|/2]$-bipancyclic whenever $d\geq4$, and also for $d\in\{2,3\}$ under explicit Hamiltonian-cycle conditions on $H_i$. Here $1\leq i\leq d$. As applications, we give sharp characterizations for undirected toroidal meshes, star-cube networks, and hyperstar networks.
item.dc:creator: Ke Lu, Ruichao Niu, Min Xu

item.title: The Hibi-Li Face-Number Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.23629v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the face-number conjecture of Hibi and Li: for every finite poset, the order polytope has no more faces of any given dimension than the chain polytope. More generally, the face numbers increase weakly along the admissible family of chain--order polytopes when one order coordinate is replaced by a chain coordinate. We also prove that, unless the order and chain polytopes are unimodularly equivalent, all face-number inequalities in dimensions $2,\ldots,|P|-1$ are strict.
item.dc:creator: Ghislain Fourier

item.title: Breaking the Infinite Barrier in the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.30888v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The balance constant is a poset parameter measuring how well random linear extensions can be split according to their relative order on two elements. We give an $\varepsilon$-improvement for the balance constant over the bound by Brightwell, Felsner and Trotter (1995), for some small $\varepsilon>0$. This is the first general result towards the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ conjecture in over 30 years.
item.dc:creator: Max Aires, Swee Hong Chan, Igor Pak, Greta Panova

item.title: Bounds for Unions of Several Parts in Balanced Graph Partitions
item.description: arXiv:2609.30927v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k\ge3$ and $1\le \ell\le k-1$. We study balanced $k$-partitions of a graph for which the union of any $\ell$ parts induces few edges. We show that every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges admits a balanced partition $V_1,\ldots,V_k$ such that \begin{equation*} \max_{\substack{A\in\binom{[k]}{\ell}}}e_G\left(\bigcup_{i\in A}V_i\right)\le\frac{\ell^2}{k^2}m+\frac{\ell^2(k-\ell)}{k^2}(n-1)+\frac{\ell(k-\ell)}{k(k-1)}\sqrt{\left(\binom{k}{\ell}-1\right)m}. \end{equation*} In the case $\ell=2$, our result confirms a conjecture of Bollob\'as and Scott in a stronger form.
item.dc:creator: Zhanping Yang

item.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
item.description: arXiv:2610.14100v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $\Lambda_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $\Lambda_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partial\Lambda_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question was left open in the previous versions; it has since been settled, $\Lambda_4=S_4$, by a computer-assisted proof of L. Marshall, after an earlier claim by D.Z. Liu, who also proved that $\Lambda_n$ is not convex for $n\ge5$. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{\pi^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $\Lambda_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Chebotarev

item.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.32192v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid, the elongated triangular grid and the snub hexagonal grid. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid. As a by-product, we prove that every identifying code of a cubic graph with the slow growth property in which every vertex lies on exactly one triangle (resp. $4$-cycle) has density at least $2/3$ (resp. $3/7$).
item.dc:creator: Rudini Sampaio

item.title: The maximum spectral radius of connected graphs with prescribed order and size
item.description: arXiv:2610.34905v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1986, Brualdi and Solheid asked which connected graph of prescribed order and size has maximum adjacency spectral radius. We complete the classification for every feasible pair of parameters. We prove that no graph outside the dense and star threshold families is extremal, including at ties, and settle the range $n\le e+1$, where the star candidate is not defined. The final comparison \emph{between} the dense and star candidates is supplied by Damnjanovi\'c's Propositions~4.1--4.2, not reproved here. We combine an exact Bellman recursion with dense-core domination, fractional complete-split bounds, and a virtual-star inequality. Three remaining comparison families (J), (K1), and (K2) are established analytically and by exact polynomial and Sturm certificates. The exact certificates are implemented in Python/SymPy and SageMath.
item.dc:creator: Dragan Stevanovi\'c

item.title: Positivity for a $t$-analogue of refined Littlewood-Richardson rules
item.description: arXiv:2610.35708v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2010, Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg proved that the product of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a Demazure atom $A_{\gamma}$ expands positively in terms of Demazure atoms, and interpreted the coefficients as the number of Littlewood-Richardson skew skyline tableaux of a given shape and a filling type. Extending this approach, they further established the positive expansion for the product of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a quasisymmetric Schur function $S_{\alpha}$, or of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a Demazure character $\kappa_{\gamma}$. In particular, the latter provides a refinement of the classical Littlewood-Richardson rule. We present a natural $t$-analogue of these positive expansions by deriving the expansion for a product of a Hall-Littlewood polynomial $P_{\lambda}(t)$ and a $t$-Demazure atom $E_{\gamma}(t)$ in terms of $t$-Demazure atoms. The corresponding coefficients are $\mathbb{N}\,[t,1-t]$-positive; that is, they are polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients in $t$ and $1-t$, and they are interpreted in terms of standard Young tableaux. We take the approach of connecting the multiplication coefficients with the LLT polynomials, which differs from the combinatorial insertion arguments of Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg.
item.dc:creator: Jiaming Du, Emma Yu Jin, Xiaowei Lin

item.title: A sparse canonical Rado theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.37053v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Canonical Ramsey theory studies structured colour patterns in colourings with arbitrarily many colours. Lefmann's canonical Rado theorem extends the canonical van der Waerden theorem of Erd\H{o}s and Graham to partition-regular linear systems. Recently, Alvarado, Kohayakawa, Morris, Mota and Ortega proved a sparse canonical van der Waerden theorem for random set $[n]_p$. In this paper, we prove a sparse canonical Rado theorem. For every irredundant partition-regular matrix $A$ of positive rank with $k\ge3$ columns, and every prescribed partition witnessing the columns condition, if $p\ge Cn^{-1/m(A)}$, then with probability at least $1-e^{-cnp}$ every colouring of $[n]_p$ contains $$\Omega\big(p^k n^{k-\rank(A)}\big)$$ canonical solutions of $A\mathbf x=0$ with distinct coordinates. A matching 0-statement holds when the prescribed partition has one or at least three blocks; the Schur equation shows that it can fail for two-block patterns. For every prescribed partition, we also establish a robust threshold at the same scale under deletion of a fixed positive proportion of the random set.
item.dc:creator: Zhenzhen Lou, Guangfu Wang, Man Wu, Zhifei Yan

item.title: Minimal doubling for small subsets in compact Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2401.14062v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an asymptotically sharp bound for the minimal doubling of a small measurable subset of a compact connected Lie group, settling a conjecture of Breuillard and Green. Namely, let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group of positive dimension $d_G$ with Haar probability measure $\mu_G$, and let $\epsilon > 0$. We show that for all compact subsets $A$ of sufficiently small measure we have \[\mu_G(A^2) \geq \left(2^{d_G-d_M} - \epsilon\right)\mu_G(A),\] where $d_M$ is the maximal dimension of a proper closed subgroup. This recovers, by a different method, the small-measure doubling theorem of Jing--Tran--Zhang for $G=\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathbb{R})$. More generally, for every $\epsilon>0$ and any pair of non-empty compact subsets $A,B$ of sufficiently small measure, we prove the Brunn--Minkowski-type inequality: \[ \mu_G(AB)^{\frac{1}{d_G-d_M}} \geq (1-\epsilon)\left( \mu_G(A)^{\frac{1}{d_G-d_M}} + \mu_G(B)^{\frac{1}{d_G-d_M}}\right).\] We also prove an inverse theorem in the semi-simple case: for any fixed $K\geq1$ and $\delta>0$, every compact $K$-approximate subgroup of sufficiently small positive Haar measure is covered by $C(d_G,K)$ translates of the $\delta$-neighbourhood of a proper closed connected subgroup. Our approach combines this inverse theorem with optimal transport and its recent applications to the Brunn--Minkowski inequality.
item.dc:creator: Simon Machado

item.title: Simple Models of Randomization and Preservation Theorems
item.description: arXiv:2408.15014v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to provide new, more uniform model-theoretic and combinatorial proofs of the preservation theorems established in [5] and [8]. More precisely, we show that randomization preserves both $NIP$ and stability: if a first-order theory $T$ has $NIP$, then so does $T^R$, and if $T$ is stable, then so is $T^R$. Our proofs rely on the systematic use of simple models of $T^R$ and quantitative combinatorial methods. In the $NIP$ case, we use indiscernible arrays and Rademacher mean width, whereas in the stable case, we use a Ramsey lemma for cross-blocks and sequential Rademacher mean width. Using simple models of $T^R$ has the advantage of allowing us to re-prove these theorems in a simpler and quantitative manner. We finally turn our attention to $NSOP$ in randomization. We show that based on the definition of $NSOP$ given in [14], $T^R$ is stable if and only if it is $NIP$ and $NSOP$.
item.dc:creator: Karim Khanaki, Massoud Pourmahdian

item.title: Amplituhedra and origami, I: tree level
item.description: arXiv:2410.09574v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a precise correspondence between points of the $m=4$ tree momentum amplituhedron and origami crease patterns. As an application, we prove that the BCFW (Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten) cells triangulate the $m=4$ tree amplituhedron both in momentum space and in momentum-twistor space. As another application, we show that every nondegenerate weighted planar bipartite graph $\Gamma$ admits a t-embedding, i.e., an embedding of the planar dual of $\Gamma$ such that the sum of angles of white (equivalently, black) faces around each vertex is equal to $\pi$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Galashin

item.title: Categorical Tiling Theory: Constructing Directed Planar Tilings via Edge Reversal
item.description: arXiv:2509.06363v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Tilings of the plane resemble the simplicial and other complexes from algebraic topology, but have not been studied from this perspective. We construct finite categories corresponding to polygons with labeled directed edges, and introduce the problem of modeling tilings of the Euclidean or hyperbolic plane as presheaves over such a category. Combinatorially, this amounts to choosing an ``alignment'' for a tiling: a direction for every edge and consistent labels for the edges of each polygonal tile. We show that for a fixed tiling, given a single alignment we can characterize every other alignment of the same tiling by comparison of the edge directions. We then construct a ``reflective'' alignment for any tiling with an even number of polygons at each vertex, and from this generate a large family of alignments with elegant symmetry properties.
item.dc:creator: Catherine DiLeo, Preston Sessoms, Brandon T. Shapiro

item.title: K\"ahler-Einstein toric submanifolds of the projective space
item.description: arXiv:2512.03617v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the K\"ahler-Einstein metrics on the four families of symmetric toric Fano manifolds due to Batyrev and Selivanova cannot be induced by immersions into projective spaces equipped with the Fubini-Study metric. We also show a similar conclusion for the non-symmetric examples discovered by Nill and Paffenholz. As an application we obtain that a centrally symmetric toric Fano manifold admits a K\"ahler-Einstein metric induced by a projective immersion if and only if it is a product of projective lines. These results confirm for each of these examples a broader conjecture characterizing the K\"ahler--Einstein metrics that can be induced by projective immersions.
item.dc:creator: Antonio J. Di Scala, Mart\'in Sombra

item.title: Quasipolynomial behavior via constructibility in multigraded algebra
item.description: arXiv:2512.18536v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Piecewise quasipolynomial growth of Presburger counting functions combines with tame persistent homology module theory to conclude piecewise quasipolynomial behavior of constructible families of finely graded modules over constructible commutative semigroup rings. Functorial preservation of constructibility for families under local cohomology, $\operatorname{Tor}$, and $\operatorname{Ext}$ yield piecewise quasipolynomial, quasilinear, or quasiconstant growth statements for length of local cohomology, $a$-invariants, regularity, depth; length of $\operatorname{Tor}$ and Betti numbers; length of $\operatorname{Ext}$ and Bass numbers; associated primes via $v$-invariants; and extended degrees, including the usual degree, Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity, arithmetic degree, and homological degree.
item.dc:creator: Hailong Dao, Ezra Miller, Jonathan Monta\~no, Christopher O'Neill, Kevin Woods

item.title: GKM Theory for Manifolds of Isospectral Matrices in Lie Type D
item.description: arXiv:2602.08366v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the manifold $Q_{\G, \lambda}$ of isospectral real skew-symmetric matrices with a prescribed sparsity pattern determined by a graph $\G$. The compact torus $T^n$ acts naturally on $Q_{\Gamma,\lambda}$ by conjugation, and this action can be studied using GKM theory. We prove two results about this manifold and its GKM graph. The first theorem describes how the GKM graph of $Q_{\G, \lambda}$ is obtained from the GKM graph of the corresponding manifold $M_{\G, \lambda}$ of isospectral Hermitian matrices. The second theorem shows that equivariant formality of $Q_{\Gamma,\lambda}$ implies equivariant formality of $M_{\Gamma,\lambda}$, whereas the converse fails.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Zhukov

item.title: Expander Evolution Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2605.12672v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce \emph{expander evolution algebras} (EEAs), a class of nonassociative algebras defined over an arbitrary field $\K$ in which the underlying undirected loopless graph of the algebra -- in the sense of Kowalski -- is an expander graph in the classical sense of Cheeger. Starting from the formal graph definition of Kowalski and the algebraic framework of Tian, we establish a dictionary between combinatorial expansion and algebraic structure: the Cheeger constant of the associated graph governs connectivity, the subalgebra lattice, the growth of the evolution sequence, and -- over $\R$ and $\C$ -- the spectral gap of the evolution operator. Over a general field $\K$ we prove that EEAs are always connected and simple (as evolution algebras), carry no proper large evolution subalgebras, and that every generator of a \emph{symmetric} EEA is algebraically persistent. Over $\C$ we obtain the sharp Alon--Boppana lower bound for the second eigenvalue of the evolution operator, leading to the definition of \emph{Ramanujan evolution algebras} as optimal expanders. We also construct families of EEAs from Cayley graphs of finite groups. We close with open problems.
item.dc:creator: Piero Giacomelli

item.title: The symmetric hit problem in four variables: Relative cohits and stabilizer-fixed preimages
item.description: arXiv:2606.02626v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we study the symmetric hit problem in four variables by analyzing the relative cohit space, defined as the kernel of the inclusion-induced map from symmetric to ordinary cohits. We establish that this relative space is isomorphic to a kernel in the first group cohomology of the permutation group and, equivalently, to an $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel for the general linear group, equipped with a canonical action of the normalizer quotient. We use explicit Lucas--Cartan identities to construct unconditional fixed Steenrod preimages for nontrivial stabilizers, resolving infinite families of monomials strictly above the minimal-spike weight. Using the ordinary and symmetric Kameko isomorphisms, we reduce the determination of complete bases in two generic degree families to exact calculations in degrees one, three, six, ten, and sixteen. The relative space first becomes nonzero in degree fifteen, where it is one-dimensional, and it is an indecomposable two-dimensional normalizer module in degree eighteen. In the family $5\cdot2^t-4$, the symmetric cohit dimension stabilizes at six and the relative dimension at one for $t\geq2$; in the family $7\cdot2^t-4$, they are four and zero for $t\geq1$. We give complete bases by explicit exponent formulas and prove Janfada's monomial implication [7, Conjecture 1] in every degree of both families. We extend the known optimal bound for ordinary Kameko isomorphisms to every permutation-invariant cohit space, prove its optimality there, and transport the entire symmetric hit basis by a direct-sum formula.
item.dc:creator: Dang Vo Phuc, Peter V. Danchev

item.title: Amplituhedra and origami, II: loop level
item.description: arXiv:2606.03439v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Building on the recently discovered origami-amplituhedron correspondence, we prove that the BCFW (Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten) cells triangulate the $m=4$ amplituhedron in full generality at all loop orders, both in momentum and momentum-twistor space. Along the way, we develop two natural "$L$-punctured" extensions of the positive Grassmannian and relate them via T-duality.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Galashin

item.title: Chromatic Constraints on Quantum Observables: Gaps, Contextuality, and Separability
item.description: arXiv:2607.04289v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Intertwined complete projective experiments share outcomes, motivating the search for a common spectral labeling across contexts. Strong coloring tests whether complete contexts admit one context-independent nondegenerate spectrum; when that labeling exists, chromatic separability tests which event distinctions it preserves. We distinguish these questions from ordinary Kochen--Specker statelessness, geometric realizability, event-order representation, and Born-probability models. A state extends to a strong d-coloring exactly when deletion of its support leaves a (d-1)-colorable graph. Faithful real 17- and 21-ray restrictions of completed Yu--Oh have separating ordinary states but forced color identities; one quantum preparation requires exactly 1/9 nonextendable weight despite admitting an ordinary-state model. Independent Hermitian projection arguments correct earlier inferences from a chromatic gap to statelessness or nonrealizability. Hesse's complex 37-ray example separates real and complex geometry and has exact state-family minima 6/7/18 for three representation requirements. A rational two-plane construction gives a linear real 65-ray example with 393,216 states and explicit event-order and probability failures. General and specified ancestry results distinguish geometric KS extensions from abstract chromatic-to-stateless constructions. Detailed enumerations, regenerated state certificates, and extended proofs are supplementary.
item.dc:creator: Karl Svozil

item.title: The list size of random linear and LDPC codes at capacity
item.description: arXiv:2609.06570v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that for every prime power $q$ and $\rho\in(0,1-\frac1q)$ there exists $\varepsilon_0(q, \rho) > 0$ such that for all positive $\varepsilon < \varepsilon_0(q, \rho)$, a random linear code over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of rate $1-h_q(\rho)-\varepsilon$ has list size $\lfloor h_q(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor$ or $\lfloor h_q(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor+1$ with probability $1-o(1)$. Before this work, the list size was known only up to a constant factor for $q\ge3$, and for $q=2$ it was known to be either $\lfloor h_2(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor-1$, $\lfloor h_2(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor$ or $\lfloor h_2(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor+1$. We also show that the same two-point concentration holds for the list size of random LDPC codes. This follows from a general theorem establishing that random LDPC codes and random linear codes have the same threshold rate for distance, list decoding, list recovery from errors and any other \emph{convex} property, which answers a question of Mosheiff, Resch, Ron-Zewi, Silas and Wootters.
item.dc:creator: Shashwat Silas

item.title: Arc Kayles is PSPACE-complete
item.description: arXiv:2609.23777v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that Arc Kayles is PSPACE-complete. This solves a question raised by Schaefer in 1976.
item.dc:creator: \'Edouard Bonnet

item.title: Refinements on the Restriction and Kakeya problems range in $\mathbb{R}^4$
item.description: arXiv:2610.06181v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We obtain improved Fourier restriction and Kakeya maximal estimates in $\mathbb R^4$. More precisely, by proving the two-ends incidence estimates $\mathbf{TE}\left(\frac{269}{89},\frac{179}{89},\frac{493}{534}\right)$ and $\mathbf{TE}(3.06\ldots,3.06\ldots,0.94\ldots)$, we extend the restriction range to $p>2+ \frac{356}{447}$ and the Kakeya maximal estimate up to dimension $3.06056$. The implications to the known lower-bounds for the Hausdorff dimension of Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and the Bochner--Riesz conjecture are also studied.
item.dc:creator: Tiago Moreira

item.title: Sums of two dependent uniform random variables: a characterization by joint tail bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.24197v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Which laws can the sum of two uniform random variables have when nothing is known about how they depend on each other? For three or more uniform summands, convex order gives the answer; for two it does not, and the question has been open. We show that the attainable laws are exactly those that satisfy a family of explicit joint bounds on sums of tail probabilities, one bound for each finite set of thresholds. For laws with a density at most one, convex order alone decides. For densities at most two, convex order implies the simplest of the joint bounds, and the constant two cannot be raised for single-threshold bounds. The number of thresholds a law needs is set by the spacing of its atoms, not by how many atoms it has.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Chaudhary, Kapil Khandelwal

item.title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
item.description: arXiv:2610.30382v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $\theta_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge \theta_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $\theta_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^\beta$, for any given $\beta\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $\theta_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.
item.dc:creator: Jacopo Borga, Victor Dubach

item.title: Complete Determination of the Gallai--van der Waerden Number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.30711v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper completely determines the Gallai--van der Waerden number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\) for all integers \(r\ge 3\): \[ \mathrm{GW}(3;3,3)=\mathrm{GW}(4;3,3)=9,\qquad \mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)=r\quad (r\ge 5). \]
item.dc:creator: Yuan Si

item.title: There are no unexpected toric positroid varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.35914v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a positroid. We prove that the positroid variety $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to some algebraic torus if and only if $\mathcal{M}$ is regular. In that case, $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to the standard diagonal torus. Thus, there are no unexpected toric positroid varieties.
item.dc:creator: Avery McNeill
